resp is stored as answered (1 to 5), not reverse-scored. Items spa_1, spa_3, spa_7, spa_11, spa_13 and spa_14 are reverse-keyed; score them as 6 - resp before summing. The study's supplement (s002.docx) gives this keying, and it reproduces the published mean (43.21), SD (10.52) and alpha (0.877). Summing the raw values gives SD 9.00 and alpha 0.805.

resp is the raw true/false answer (0/1), not the scored SAD. To reproduce the published SAD total (mean 13.68, SD 7.47, r = 0.195 with expressive suppression), score sad_2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 24 and 26 as 1 - resp and sum all 28. Pooled from MECO L1's two collection rounds, which are different people at mostly different sites: cov_sample 1 = wave 1 (13 sites), 2 = wave 2 (16 sites). It is not a panel, so the round is cov_sample rather than wave. cov_language is the language and cov_site the release's site code. The 42 wave-1 Norwegian readers answered 47 questions (text 6 question 4 was not administered).

Item codes are shared only where the question is the same. Only texts 1, 3, 7, 11 and 12 are translations of a common original (the authors' is.matched flag); their questions are text{t}_q{q} across sites. The other 7 texts were written per language, so their items carry a language or text-version prefix (e.g. du_text2_q1) and are answered only by that site's readers: the table is sparse by design, with a median of 45 readers per item. A version is shared across sites or rounds only where the text is identical (no and tr across rounds, en with en_uk, the two Hindi sites except text 5, German wave 2 as ge_v2, sp with sp_ch on texts 2, 4, 5 and 9). Eight wave-1 matched questions that are a different question in that language get site-specific codes (ee_text3_q1, ee_text3_q2, sp_text3_q3, he_text1_q3, he_text12_q4, ru_text12_q4, gr_text12_q2, tr_text12_q3).

Wave 2 published no comprehension-question wording, so for wave-2 sites the equivalence of the matched questions (text{t}_q{q}) is assumed from the authors' design and is unverified. Two wave-2 sites contradict it in their responses and are coded site-specific instead: ru_mo for all 48 items (its per-question accuracy does not match any other site, nor wave-1 Russian on identical texts) and ba for text 11.

Three studies of the same paired-choice task, pooled; cov_sample names the study. LargeValence_2017 and LargeValence_2018 share 7 pictures (Cat, Crow, Doctor, Fire, Frustrated, Lake, War); LowValence_2017 uses 7 others (Flowers, Food, Grass, House, Monkey, Sunset, Timber). No one saw both sets, so the two halves share no items. Each trial is two rows: resp 1 for the picture chosen, 0 for the one passed over; trial numbers restart within each study.

The CASEN time-use follow-ups (u1_a to u11_a, u15_a to u17_a: minutes per day spent on each activity, 0 to 1440) are not included. They are measured quantities, not item responses. The yes/no and rating items they follow (u1 to u22) are all here.

Item codes are the survey's. b1a-b4: ASER tool, adaptive (b1c, b2, b3, b4 are asked only on certain earlier outcomes, so they have few rows; b4 has 2). c = written abstract, d = oral abstract, e = oral anchored (word problem); the digit is the operation (1 add, 2 subtract, 3 multiply, 4 divide) and _v1-_v4 the survey version. Each child got one version, and versions use different numbers, so c1_v1 and c1_v2 are different items. f1 = oral anchored market problem; f2 = pretend market, scored as the authors do (a total within rounding of the exact one counts). Division answers within a rounding band count as correct, per the enumerators' coding. The randomised-hint follow-up to f1 is not included.

Study 3a wave 1 only, first attempts only. Each child solved one of two variants of each subtraction and division problem (randomised); the item code names the operands. The mystery-shopping and hypothetical-market questions are not included (each uses the child's own goods and prices, so no two children answer the same item), nor are second attempts and post-hint attempts (asked only after a wrong answer or under a randomised hint). Study 3a wave 2 is a different instrument and is not here. cov_market is the authors' corrected market id.

resp scores the annotator's choice against the CIFAR-10 ground-truth label (itemcov_true_category), which is itself a label assigned when the dataset was built and is wrong for some images; Peterson et al. (2019) use the human label distribution, not the key, as the target. The chosen class is in resp_raw (core) and text (cifar10h_nom).

text is not an option the student chose: it is the graders' classification of the free-text answer (in answer_text) into one of five accuracy categories, converted from finer facet-level annotations and hand-revised by the task organisers. resp collapses it to SemEval's 2-way scheme (1 = correct, 0 = any other label). id is module_student: student numbers restart in each module, and each module was given to a different group of children.

Forfeited games: winner follows Retrosheet's forfeit code, not the score (forfeit V = agent_b, H = agent_a; T, ruled a no-decision, = draw). homefield is always agent_a, the team Retrosheet lists as home; neutral-site games (Tokyo, London, Mexico City series, etc.) are not marked, and park identifies them. league NAssn is Retrosheet's NA (National Association, 1871-75), renamed so it is not read as missing.

agent_a is always the winning team (the source records only winner and loser, not side or serve), so winner is always agent_a; do not read an agent_a advantage into it. Agents are doubles teams keyed by their two pklmart player ids. Data are player-entered, mostly amateur games, and sparse: most teams appear in one game.

excluded = 1 marks the decisions of judges whose median time per judgement was under 5 seconds (484 of 3,969). Sangwin & Kinnear dropped these as nonserious judges, and their analyses and the Kinnear et al. CJ meta-analysis use the remaining 3,485.

Raters who were not logged in to Zooniverse (rater_logged_in = 0, 67,558 decisions) are identified per browser session, so one person may appear as several raters. The two sessions show the same 1,111 images, the second after brightness equalisation; analyse them separately or model session.

No game ends in a draw. Under SSCAIT's rules a crashing bot loses (crashed names it, 3,538 games), and a game that hits the time limit (90 in-game minutes, or 5 minutes with no unit dying) goes to the bot with the higher kills+razings score (timelimit = 1, 1,437 games; the API notes these as "draw;"). Filter on both if only games played to destruction are wanted.

Wikipedia prints each score without saying whose comes first, so score_a/score_b give the higher score to the listed winner. Matches before about 1890 were decided on goals: 58 have no points score (score_a/score_b blank, printed score in score_raw), and the early points values are as the pages give them. Home side is the venue's country (Belfast counts as Ireland); World Cup and other third-country matches have homefield blank. Only matches both sides capped are included: the 1920-28 Australia (New South Wales) v New Zealand and South Africa matches and uncapped touring XVs are excluded.

resp runs in the opposite direction to the source's SPSS file and paper: here 1 = 'No! Totally disagree!' through 5 = 'Yes! Totally agree!', whereas the deposit codes 1 = 'Yes! Totally agree!' through 5 = 'No! Totally disagree!' on all eleven items. IRW numbers the response labels from least to most agreement, as for this study's other scales. To join resp back to the deposit or read it with the deposit's codebook, use 6 - resp.

rating = "On a scale from 1 to 7, where 1 indicates that your state should absolutely not admit the migrant and 7 indicates that your state should definitely admit the migrant, how would you rate Migrant 1/2?"; choice = which of the two the respondent would prefer be allowed to stay (forced, no opt-out). choice = which applicant the respondent would prefer be allowed to stay (forced, no opt-out); rating 1 (absolutely send back) to 7 (definitely allow to stay). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Attribute order varied by one of four undocumented schemes (trial_attribute_order). 7 respondents with no answers dropped; 8 implausible ages (above 100) blanked.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which strike option (Option 1 / Option 2) the respondent chose; wording not deposited; forced choice, no opt-out; 1,439 unanswered pairs omitted. Level text is the authors' short labels; survey weights in cov_survey_weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). No choice question. Unanswered tasks (207) omitted; the authors' derived dummies and an unlabelled education code dropped.

Refused/don't know (504 rows) dropped; 4,975 respondents fielded, 4,920 with an answer; vignette wording and interview language not in the deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is a forced choice of the preferred trade agreement (wording paraphrased in the article; instrument appendix not available), no opt-out. One respondent with no regime values dropped; Qualtrics IDs, timings and the authors' derived dummies dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is which of two candidates the respondent would be more likely to support (no opt-out described; 2,430 tasks unanswered, choice blank); rating and rating_mobilize are 5-point candidate-rating and mobilization items stored in the authors' recode (higher = more favourable; wording and anchors not deposited). Attribute levels are the authors' English coding labels, not the Korean text shown. Occupation levels are unequal (accuser and accused occupation unemployed on about 8% of profiles each). cov_gender is the investigator's gender (female/male). Unanswered pairs omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: choice of one of two criminal opportunities (Stata label "Criminal opportunity chosen"; question wording not deposited); forced choice, no opt-out. Task and profile are inferred from row order; 18 unanswered tasks omitted. Attribute text comes from Stata value labels; randomization restrictions undocumented. The deposit has 1,000 respondents, the article reports 1,023.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is a forced choice between two nominees (24 unanswered tasks blank) and rating a 1-5 rating of each, wording and anchors not deposited (5 = favourable inferred from agreement with choice). Randomization restricted: party constrains ideology (no Democratic conservative or Republican liberal), and race and law-school levels have unequal weights. Task and profile inferred from row blocks; YouGov IDs re-keyed; cov_survey_weight is the YouGov weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three profiles per task: choice = which participant the respondent thought would give the most to the common pool (forced, one of three); rating = expected contribution 0-10 in units of DKK 100. Between-respondent information conditions (trial_information) add socio-economic, cultural-value, norm-compliance, all, or placebo attributes; attributes not shown are (not shown). Danish-named profiles were born in Denmark 90% of the time, Middle Eastern-named 50%. attr_name_origin is the author's grouping of attr_name. All profiles are men. cov_survey_weight is the YouGov weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which intervention was the MOST successful?" (forced, no opt-out; 43 pairs unanswered); rating: "How successful were each of the interventions?" 1 = Very Unsuccessful .. 4 = Very Successful. Task and profile inferred from row order. Level text is the deposit's value labels (may abbreviate the displayed wording); restrictions undocumented. cov_attention_pass flags the pre-treatment attention check used in the authors' robustness check.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four forced choices between two electoral-reform scenarios per task (Scenario 1/2, no opt-out): choice = "If you had to choose one of these scenarios, which would you pick?"; choice_voice, choice_governability (1 = scenario judged to make legislation more difficult to pass) and choice_responsiveness. Attribute order randomized by respondent (attrpos_*); the ideology attribute was a graph, stored as its lead sentence plus the authors' label. Qualtrics IDs and free text dropped; 2,177 respondents and 12,842 rows as in the Supplementary Material.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate for Congress would you support in this Democratic Primary election?" (Candidate A/B, forced, no opt-out); one task per respondent. Restricted randomization: one candidate always Black, one White; no shared endorsement. Deposit contains white respondents only. Ratings stored 0-1 as deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate for Congress would you support in this Democratic Primary election?" (Candidate A/B, forced, no opt-out); one task per respondent. Restricted randomization: one candidate always Black, one White; no shared endorsement. Deposit contains white respondents only (all parties; the paper analyses Democrats: cov_party_id7 Lean, Mostly or Strong Democrat). Ratings stored 0-1 as deposited. Profile order inferred from row order. One respondent with no answers dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate for Congress would you support in this Democratic Primary election?" (Candidate A/B, forced, no opt-out); one task per respondent. Restricted randomization: one candidate always Black, one White; no shared endorsement. Deposit contains white respondents only (all parties; the paper analyses Democrats: cov_party_id7 Lean, Mostly or Strong Democrat). Profile order inferred from row order. One respondent with no choice dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate for Congress would you support in this Democratic Primary election?" (Candidate A/B, forced, no opt-out); one task per respondent. Restricted randomization: one candidate always Black, one White; no shared endorsement. Deposit contains white respondents only (all parties; the paper analyses Democrats: cov_party_id7 Lean, Mostly or Strong Democrat). Profile order inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which scenario was selected as preferred (wording not deposited), forced choice, no opt-out. Attribute levels are associated and unequal in the data (pre-generated choice design), so estimate with all attributes in the model. Level text rebuilt from dummies with codebook wording (English; display language undocumented); the codebook's attribute names for A3/A4 are swapped relative to the Stata labels, which were followed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is a forced choice between two job offers and rating a 5-point rating of each offer (the authors' recode of the raw Qualtrics codes; higher = more favourable inferred; wording not deposited). Attribute levels are the authors' labels, and the backsliding levels are their code names for statements respondents read. IP addresses, locations and Qualtrics IDs dropped; unanswered tasks omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is a forced choice between two job offers and rating a 5-point rating of each offer (the authors' recode of the raw Qualtrics codes; higher = more favourable inferred; wording not deposited). Attribute levels are the authors' labels, and the backsliding levels are their code names for statements respondents read. IP addresses, locations and Qualtrics IDs dropped; unanswered tasks omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which candidate the respondent would vote for (Congress wording: 'If you had to choose between them, which of these candidates would you vote to be a member of the U.S. House of Representatives?'; presidential wording not deposited), forced choice, no opt-out. Attributes independently randomized (level probabilities not stated); attribute order randomized per respondent, not recorded. Tasks 1-5 are President and 6-10 Congress for all, though the block order was randomized, so task order is not display order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two candidates the respondent chose in a hypothetical nonpartisan local election (wording not deposited); forced, no opt-out. Task order inferred from row order (five stacked blocks of the same respondents); profile recorded. The article says levels were uniform with no restrictions, but White-coded names appear about three times as often as each Black- or Latino-coded name. CES covariates kept as codes, except cov_gender and cov_party_id (text); cov_survey_weight blank for 308 respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = reported callback for each resume (1 = would call back, 0 = no), each resume judged on its own; no choice question. Study-group attribute blocked within respondent (each saw comic, socialism and Western groups once); other attributes binary. Level text is paraphrase from the ReadMe; task order inferred from row order; income missing for 36 respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three ratings of each applicant, 1-10, higher = more: rating_merit (academic merit), rating_connections (strength of government connections), rating_conformity (political conformity to the CCP regime); no choice question. Three binary attributes; randomization rules not documented. Wording is the ReadMe's paraphrase; task order = profile letter, display order undocumented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which candidate would you be more likely to vote for?" (A or B, no opt-out; 2,632 tasks unanswered, left blank); rating_ideology: candidate placement 0 = Left .. 10 = Right; rating_represent: "Candidate A/B represents people who are under-represented in politics" 0 = strongly disagree .. 4 = strongly agree. Each respondent saw a no-party and a party pair in random order (trial_party_shown; attr_party (not shown) when not shown). Gender and minority status were signalled by names not in the deposit (codebook codings kept); disability and minority names had non-uniform weights. 6,011 ids in the deposit vs N=3,000 per country reported; 42 with no answers dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two MPs the respondent would vote for (forced choice, no opt-out; wording paraphrased from the preprint). Restriction: AfD candidates always have two years in parliament, so party and experience effects must be estimated within allowed combinations. Attribute order randomized (attrpos_*). Half the respondents answered the survey questions before the conjoint (trial_block_order). Level and covariate text is German as displayed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice is the preferred restaurant in each of 5 pairs (exact wording not deposited); forced choice, no opt-out. Task and profile are inferred from row order. Level text is the .dta value labels; the deposit's Data Dictionary gives the staff-composition codes the other way round and labels the worst review 'Terrible', so those two attributes carry some label uncertainty. cov_survey_weight is the YouGov weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which borrower most deserves to have a significant portion of their student loan debt forgiven (forced, no opt-out); rating = how deserving each borrower is, 1 Very Undeserving to 5 Very Deserving. Only tasks 1-4 are kept: the deposit records race only for those, whether race was shown in tasks 5-6 is undocumented, and the authors analyse tasks 1-4. The authors' code gives profile B profile A's repayment history; this table carries the correct value, so its AMCEs differ slightly from the published ones.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two partner countries the respondent prefers Costa Rica to choose for a trade agreement (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = support for an agreement with each country, 1 not support at all to 7 strongly support. Full independent randomization; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. Level text is the authors' English labels, not the Spanish shown; 266 tasks dropped (political system missing in 311 rows; 13 tasks with no choice).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two partner countries the respondent prefers Nicaragua to choose for a trade agreement (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = support for an agreement with each country, 1 not support at all to 7 strongly support. Full independent randomization; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. Level text is the authors' English labels, not the Spanish shown; 786 tasks dropped (economic size missing for task 5 profile 1 of 536 respondents; political system missing in 335 rows).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Outcome: forced choice of the district the respondent would prefer to vote in (paraphrase; verbatim Spanish question not deposited), no opt-out. Task and profile are inferred from row order. Attribute text is the authors' short English labels (display language not documented, presumably Spanish); the deposit's Networks levels do not match the article's Table 1, so labels were not mapped. 1,200 respondents as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Na ktorego kandydata najprawdopodobniej zaglosowal(a)bys?" (which candidate would you most likely vote for), forced, no opt-out; rating: "Jak oceniasz profil kandydata A/B?" 1 = strongly disapprove .. 7 = strongly approve (codebook's 1-6 is wrong). Attribute order randomized per task (not recorded); candidate gender weighted 35% female. Includes all 2,910 respondents but one with no attributes; the article's analytic sample (1,979) drops inattentive respondents and speeders: cov_attention_pass_1 / cov_attention_pass_2 carry the authors' attention flags; covariates blank for 287 respondents not in the survey file.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the profile the respondent identified as the "illegal" (trial_condition = illegal) or "undocumented" (trial_condition = undocumented) immigrant, a perception judgement, not a preference; verbatim instruction not deposited. No opt-out documented; 40 of 6,498 tasks with no chosen profile were dropped, removing 3 of 1,083 respondents. Police record and benefits levels were not equally likely (about half No record / None; 2 labelled police-record levels never occur). Attribute text is the authors' value labels.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating is how typical the profiled person is of welfare recipients, 0-10 (higher = more typical; a stereotype-content rating, not a preference), one profile per task, 30 tasks; no choice question. Attribute order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_*); levels independently drawn. The table keeps all 1,964 respondents; the article analyses 1,271 non-Hispanic white respondents (cov_ethnicity == 1 and cov_hispanic == 1) with non-constant ratings. 72 missing ratings omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "¿Cuál de las dos personas preferiría usted que pague una tasa de impuestos más alta?" (forced choice of one of two; skipped tasks omitted); choice = 1 marks the person chosen to pay MORE tax (unfavourable, kept as asked). Attributes fully randomized per the article; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 1,688 respondents with an answer kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the author's 1,527 (finished, consented, not speeding), matching the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of the two individuals would you personally prefer to charge a higher tax rate to?" (forced choice of one of two; skipped tasks omitted); choice = 1 marks the person chosen to pay MORE tax (unfavourable, kept as asked). Attributes fully randomized per the article; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 1,633 respondents with an answer kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the author's 1,450 (finished, consented, not speeding), matching the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "¿Cuál de las dos personas preferiría usted que pague una tasa de impuestos más alta?" (forced choice of one of two; skipped tasks omitted); choice = 1 marks the person chosen to pay MORE tax (unfavourable, kept as asked). Attributes fully randomized per the article; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 1,584 respondents with an answer kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the author's 1,418 (finished, consented, not speeding), matching the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of the two individuals would you personally prefer to charge a higher tax rate to?" (forced choice of one of two; skipped tasks omitted); choice = 1 marks the person chosen to pay MORE tax (unfavourable, kept as asked). Attributes fully randomized per the article; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 2,081 respondents with an answer kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the author's 1,946 (finished, consented, not speeding), matching the article. US weights not deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two climate agreements the respondent prefers (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = "If you could vote on each of these agreements in a referendum, how likely is it that you would vote in favor or against each of the agreements?" from 1 (definitely against) to 10 (definitely in favor), stored unrescaled. One of four country tables (Germany); costs and sanctions are this country's displayed amounts, other levels are the article's English text; dimension order was randomized but its code is undocumented and not kept; profile position is inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two climate agreements the respondent prefers (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = "If you could vote on each of these agreements in a referendum, how likely is it that you would vote in favor or against each of the agreements?" from 1 (definitely against) to 10 (definitely in favor), stored unrescaled. One of four country tables (France); costs and sanctions are this country's displayed amounts, other levels are the article's English text; dimension order was randomized but its code is undocumented and not kept; profile position is inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two climate agreements the respondent prefers (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = "If you could vote on each of these agreements in a referendum, how likely is it that you would vote in favor or against each of the agreements?" from 1 (definitely against) to 10 (definitely in favor), stored unrescaled. One of four country tables (United Kingdom); costs and sanctions are this country's displayed amounts, other levels are the article's English text; dimension order was randomized but its code is undocumented and not kept; profile position is inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two climate agreements the respondent prefers (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = "If you could vote on each of these agreements in a referendum, how likely is it that you would vote in favor or against each of the agreements?" from 1 (definitely against) to 10 (definitely in favor), stored unrescaled. One of four country tables (United States); costs and sanctions are this country's displayed amounts, other levels are the article's English text; dimension order was randomized but its code is undocumented and not kept; profile position is inferred from row order.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'If you had to choose between these two candidates in the upcoming primary, who would you vote for? If neither of the two candidates appeals to you, please still indicate who you would rather vote for.' (forced choice, no opt-out). Candidates shown as prose; attributes are job, office, polls and four campaign statements drawn from lists of 12, 12, 8 and 8 (online appendix Table B1). Randomization restrictions undocumented (shares look uniform). The authors' derived populism codings and populist-attitude flags are dropped; cov_attention_pass flags the respondents who passed the attention check.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which person the respondent selected as more Black (Person A/B, forced; wording not deposited); rating = how Black each person is, 0 = Not at all to 10 = Very. Four forms randomized between respondents: parents' race shown or not (attr_parents = '(not shown)' when not shown; trial_ancestry_shown) and skin tone near the top or at the bottom (trial_skin_tone_row). Authors' filters applied (2,397 respondents; README's 2,385 excludes 12 outside the three race groups); 2 tasks without saved levels dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which proposal do you find most appropriate?', forced, no opt-out; rating = 'How much confidence would you have in this new organization if created as proposed?', 1 = none at all to 7 = a lot of confidence. Four Yes/No attributes (which groups get a lot of say), randomly drawn from the 16 combinations; between-subject vignette factors (government participation, scope, costs and benefits) in trial_ fields. Four countries pooled with the authors' weight; covariates in the deposit cannot be linked to respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which proposal do you find most appropriate?', forced, no opt-out; rating = 'How much confidence would you have in this new organization if created as proposed?', 1 = none at all to 7 = a lot of confidence. Four Yes/No attributes (which groups get a lot of say), randomly drawn from the 16 combinations; between-subject vignette factors (government participation, scope, costs and benefits) in trial_ fields. Four countries pooled with the authors' weight; covariates in the deposit cannot be linked to respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = 'Would you vote for these candidates?' and rating_win = 'Do you think these candidates could win local election?', each asked of both candidates (1 = yes, 0 = no; one, both or neither), translated from the Ukrainian/Russian survey. Attribute order below the name randomized per respondent (attrpos_). A 25-year-old never has 15 years of experience (the authors' design file also excludes age 35 with 15 years, but the data contain it). 46 speeders dropped as in the paper; N = 2,155 matches.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). For each of two autocratic countries per task respondents said whether they would support US military intervention, economic sanctions and democracy aid (rating_military_intervention, rating_economic_sanctions, rating_democracy_aid; 1 = yes, 0 = no; any number of tools or none), so there is no choice between profiles. Attribute row order was randomized per task and is recorded in attrpos_; task 5 of the 101 wave-2 records is dropped because its levels were not saved. The deposit's 1,591 records (2017) exceed the article's 1,464 (dated 2016).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the individual judged more likely to violate public-health guidelines ("quale dei due individui sarebbe più probabile di violare le linee guida di sanità pubblica?"; forced, no opt-out; being chosen is unfavourable, kept as asked). Italian level text as displayed; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). Questions Q15.3 and Q15.5 displayed randomizer sets F-3 and F-2; task = question order with the profiles actually shown (trial_profile_set), whereas the authors' code pairs them the other way round. A rare birthplace level 'Africa' (83 profiles) is kept (the authors drop it). All 2,734 respondents with an answer kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the authors' two-wave sample (1,237).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the individual who should get vaccine priority ("quale dei seguenti cittadini italiani dovrebbe avere la priorità secondo lei?"; forced, no opt-out). Italian level text as displayed (accents stripped in the export restored for 'Più di 80' and 'Povertà'); attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). All 1,268 respondents kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the authors' two-wave sample (1,236).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'PER CHI VOTEREBBE?' (who would you vote for), Candidato A or B, forced, no opt-out. Fixed set of 27 pairs (54 profiles) shown in random order, not independently randomized, so attribute levels are correlated across the design; task is the display position and trial_contest the pair number. Italian displayed text, opinion quotes without quotation marks; 23 unanswered pairs omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the scenario chosen (perceived chance of Taiwan's victory; exact wording and display language not in the deposit), forced, exactly one per task. Levels are the authors' short English labels. Randomization rules and attribute order not documented. 1,444 respondents as in the authors' run.log.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the scenario chosen (perceived chance of Taiwan's victory; exact wording and display language not in the deposit), forced, exactly one per task. Levels are the authors' short English labels. Randomization rules and attribute order not documented. 1,011 respondents as in the authors' run.log.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Based on the information provided, please select the aspirant that you would prefer to place on a prominent placement in your party's candidate list" (article's English rendering; Kandidat A/B, forced, no opt-out). Fully randomized profiles; the share of women already on the list (10-50%) is randomized per task and stored as trial_list_share. Ideology levels are relative ('Etwas linker/rechter/moderater als Sie') with wording that depends on the respondent's left/centre/right group. 1,856 respondents incl. non-selectors; cov_in_authors_sample = the article's 1,389 (1,343 with at least one choice).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the preferred of two hypothetical election-calling scenarios (`selected`, exactly one per task; question wording not in the deposit). 8 attributes, Japanese text shown; attribute order not recorded. Remaining term 0 occurs only with reason 'full term' (任期満了のため) and vice versa. Counts not checked against the article (not retrievable).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = the preferred of two hypothetical election-calling scenarios (`selected`, exactly one per task; question wording not in the deposit). 8 attributes, Japanese text shown; attribute order not recorded. Remaining term 0 occurs only with how-decided 'term expired' (任期満了のため) and vice versa; reason 'full term' only with remaining term 0. The authors' code also forbids term 0 with other reasons, but 2,179 such profiles occur in the data (flagged). Counts not checked against the article (not retrievable).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice_meeting = which of two organizations (A/B) the respondent would rather attend meetings of (paraphrase of the abstract), choice_scandal = organization picked in the scandal question (wording not deposited; picking is unfavourable, the author reverses it), both forced A/B, no opt-out. Level text from the codebook in English, display language undocumented; restrictions and attribute order undocumented. 13 profiles with an unsaved attribute value have their task dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "which of these two immigrants would you personally prefer to see admitted to the United States?" and choice_values = "which ... do you think has greater shared values with the United States?" (forced choice, no opt-out); rating and rating_values are 1-7 ratings of admission (1 = absolutely not admit, 7 = definitely admit) and of shared values (1 = none, 7 = a great deal). Levels are the phrases embedded in written descriptions; no randomization restrictions are documented. 1,621 respondents after the authors' filters (article: 1,650).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = 'How likely or unlikely do you think you would be to vote for each candidate from the [Democratic/Republican] Party instead of the candidate from the [Republican/Democratic] Party in each of the two elections?' (party filled per respondent; Very Unlikely = 1 to Very Likely = 7). The two candidates in a pair are not competing against each other. Arms: fully randomized vs constrained (only Scandal differs within a pair); in both arms exactly one candidate per pair has the scandal. Attribute order randomized per respondent and recorded. Respondents who failed the attention checks are kept and flagged (cov_attention_pass_1 = Q4.1, which the authors use to drop respondents; cov_attention_pass_2 = Q36.1).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = 'How likely are you to purchase shoe 1?' (asked for shoe 1 and shoe 2; Very Unlikely = 1 to Very Likely = 7). Four arms (trial_design): in 'random' arms all attributes vary, in 'constrained' arms only the focal attribute (Eco-Friendly Materials for treat, Gel Cushioning for control) differs between the two shoes; in every arm the focal attribute always differs within a pair. Attribute order randomized per respondent and recorded. One MTurk worker who answered twice dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which app would you be more likely to install on your phone?' (Mobile App 1 / Mobile App 2), forced choice, no opt-out. Restriction observed: a decentralised app always has 'Not stored', 'Notify users directly', and no contacts or location uploaded, and those storage/purpose levels never occur with a central database. Attribute order randomized and recorded (attrpos_). Preview/pre-launch responses and screened-out respondents dropped as by the authors; N = 1,504 matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which household arrangement the respondent would personally prefer to be in (paraphrase; forced choice, no opt-out); rating = 'How FAIR do you think Couple A's/B's situation is?' 1 = very unfair to 5 = very fair. Attribute levels are the phrases inserted into a vignette whose template is not deposited. 8 tasks whose levels were not saved and 24 tasks with no choice dropped (1,938 -> 1,935 respondents); the article reports nearly 2,000 parents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which side do you sympathize more with: Group A or Group B?" forced, no opt-out. The two groups always differ on every binary attribute (mirror images); task 11 repeats task 1 with sides swapped (trial_repeat_of = 1), used by the authors for reliability correction. All 1,253 panel completes kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the authors' 1,198 (their kept-id list; the deposited fraud-flag rule alone does not reproduce it). IP, geolocation and panel ids dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which side do you sympathize more with: Group A or Group B?" forced, no opt-out; choice_similar_palestinian / choice_similar_israeli: which group is more similar to actual Palestinian groups (pairs 1-5) / the actual Israeli government (pairs 6-10), asked later about the same pairs, kept as asked (the authors flip the Palestinian item). The two groups always differ on every binary attribute (mirror images); task 11 repeats task 1 with sides swapped (trial_repeat_of = 1), used by the authors for reliability correction. All 1,104 panel completes kept; cov_in_authors_sample marks the authors' 1,001 (their kept-id list; the deposited fraud-flag rule alone does not reproduce it). IP, geolocation and panel ids dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two hypothetical Russian individuals the respondent preferred to help (article paraphrase; verbatim wording not deposited), forced choice, no opt-out, 2 tasks. Attributes independently randomized (article); level text is the authors' English labels, respondents saw Russian. Authors' derived binaries and Russian-text fields dropped; N = 2,036 matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of these two candidates do you prefer?' (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = 'On a scale from 0 to 100, how competent do you think these candidates would be as mayor?' (0-100, higher = more competent). Attributes fully randomized; whether party is shown is randomized per election (trial_election; attr_party = '(not shown)' when not shown). Profile order is inferred from row order; attribute order was randomized and not recorded. MTurk worker ID dropped and respondents re-keyed; one worker with two sets of contests and 4 contests left with one row by the authors' na.omit dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of these two candidates do you prefer?' (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = 'On a scale from 0 to 100, how competent do you think these candidates would be as mayor?' (0-100, higher = more competent). Competence is missing for some candidates (127 respondents never rated). Attributes fully randomized; whether party is shown is randomized per election (trial_election; attr_party = '(not shown)' when not shown). Profile order is inferred from row order; attribute order was randomized and not recorded. Up to 5 contests per respondent (some fewer in the deposit).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Forestil dig, at du tilbydes følgende to poster som medlem af byrådet. ... Hvilken post vil du vælge?" (Mulighed A/B, forced, no opt-out). Levels are the Danish text shown; the position wording varies with the respondent's municipality type (Borgmester/Rådmand/Udvalgsformand). Simple randomization; position always first, the other three attributes in a per-respondent random order (attrpos_*). 2,141 respondents incl. partial completers; cov_in_authors_sample = the authors' complete-and-on-time filter, 1,939 respondents vs 1,938 in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Of these two projects, which one do you prefer?" (forced, no opt-out); rating = support for each project if your city were evaluating it, 1 = no support at all to 7 = complete support (English translation of the Chinese questionnaire). Levels are the Chinese text shown; attribute order randomized per task (attrpos_*). Waves 1 (Nov 2014) and 2 (Oct 2015) pooled with trial_wave as the authors do. Task and profile are inferred from the stacked file layout; 4 tasks with unsaved attribute text dropped; 2,846 respondents (2,224 + 622 as reported).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Each respondent rated one candidate; rating = vote for the candidate and rating_* = nine further judgements of the same candidate, all 0-10 (anchors and exact wording not deposited; names paraphrase the authors' variables; 98/99 don't know/refused set to NA). Four binary attributes; level text is the authors' value labels, not the displayed vignette prose. Saudi Arabia and Yemen pilot respondents dropped as by the authors; 507 respondents with no outcome omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-profile design: rating = agreement that 'The company's decision to introduce the new technology is fair', rating_ceo = would make the same decision as CEO, both 1 = strongly disagree to 5 = strongly agree (don't know missing). Only the specific-information arm (2/3 of 8,033) saw tables; price levels are conditional on the product (same / 20% / 50% cheaper) and the low-skilled count never stays at 200, so estimate within those restrictions; wages are in local currency. 20 respondents whose attribute values were not saved are dropped; the policy items (cov_policy_*) were asked after the tables.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two candidates the respondent would have preferred to win a seat in the European Parliament (forced choice, no opt-out; article's English). Levels are the authors' English labels (respondents saw Italian); all 3,096 respondents are kept, including 420 who saw the rare 'artisan' job level that the article's main analysis (n = 2,676) excludes; the 7-point rating is not built because only a dichotomized version was deposited. Attribute order was randomized but not recorded; cov_attention_pass flags the authors' attention subsample.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Image conjoint of vote tally sheets; attributes are the author's coding of six manipulated features. choice: which of two sheets has "more reliable information about the vote outcomes" (forced, no opt-out); rating_misconduct 1 = very unlikely .. 5 = very likely misconduct occurred, and four 1-5 agree items (tally changed, party interests unprotected, party influence, officer pressure); all ratings: higher = more suspicion, kept as asked. Clean and corrected images came from separate pools (non-uniform combinations); 21 tasks with identical feature sets are kept (the author drops them, 2,298 rows). Vote numbers on the images not stored.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-profile ratings of hypothetical Bundestag members, 1 = stimme gar nicht zu .. 7 = stimme voll und ganz zu: rating_voter_interest (primarily represents voters' interests), rating_competent, rating_own_interest (primarily represents own or third-party interests; higher = less favourable, kept as asked), rating_hardworking; wording paraphrased from truncated labels. Outside activity and income shown as one line (13 levels; 'none' 25%, others about 6% each); party shares follow 2021 vote shares. 3 respondents failing the attention check kept with cov_attention_pass = 0; cov_survey_weight = the authors' weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two job offers was most attractive / more likely to be accepted (paraphrase), forced choice, no opt-out; rating = attractiveness of each offer, 1 = Not at all attractive to 5 = Very attractive (the authors' recode of the raw Qualtrics codes). Attributes fully randomized (article); level text from the article's example trial and notes, with the two Trump political-climate levels and two location levels not seen displayed. Demographics other than birth year, 7-point party ID and COVID concern dropped (unlabelled); N = 984 (article: about 1,000).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = chosen candidate, forced choice; question wording not in the deposit. Party always shown, plus a random 1-9 of nine other attributes per task ('(not shown)' = not shown; trial_information_condition); party level rebuilt from the authors' copartisan flag. Level shares are unequal (e.g. Male 67%, Lawyer 30%), not documented. 69 tasks with no recorded choice dropped (1,059 -> 1,037 respondents); N vs the paper not checked (paywalled).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = against which of the two countries military action is more justified (paraphrase; forced choice); rating = justification of military action against each country, 0 = Completely unjustified to 10 = Completely justified. Mass (Lucid) and State Department expert samples pooled with cov_sample. Task is inferred from row order; 132 tasks with no recorded choice are blank (the authors count them as not chosen); 57 rows with no outcome dropped, leaving 1,131 respondents vs 1,132 reported.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two patients the respondent would prioritize for intensive care (forced choice, no opt-out; wording paraphrased from the preprint, not deposited); 2,053 unanswered pairs omitted. Arrival is randomized for patient A only and patient B's arrival follows from it. Level text is the authors' English labels; respondents saw English, German, Italian, Polish or Portuguese screens. Partisanship names a different left/right party per country (cov_country). The country-size weight and derived party-rating variables are dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = 'Given the information available, what is your best estimate about whether Country A will stand firm in this dispute, ranging form 0 percent to 100 percent?' (0-100, higher = more likely to stand firm); choice = which of the two countries is more likely to stand firm (forced choice, no opt-out; the article quotes only the Kertzer et al. wording it adopted). No restrictions on combinations (so 'the United States' can be 'a dictatorship'). Level text is the appendix sentence fragments; the wide popularity columns are coded opposite to the long label and the long label is followed. Authors' inattention flags dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which profile would you prefer to have as your next-door neighbour?" (Neighbour A/B, forced, no opt-out; English master wording, shown translated). Levels are the panel file's short English labels. Non-uniform level weights and party-ideology restrictions per the questionnaire; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. cov_in_authors_sample = 0 for respondents without the right to vote, whom the authors drop (975 of 977 kept by them; counts match their files exactly).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which profile would you prefer to have as your next-door neighbour?" (Neighbour A/B, forced, no opt-out; English master wording, shown translated). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which profile would you prefer to have as your next-door neighbour?" (Neighbour A/B, forced, no opt-out; English master wording, shown translated). Non-uniform level weights and party-ideology restrictions per the questionnaire; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. cov_in_authors_sample = 0 for respondents without the right to vote, whom the authors drop (986 of 997 kept by them; counts match their files exactly).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which profile would you prefer to have as your next-door neighbour?" (Neighbour A/B, forced, no opt-out; English master wording, shown translated). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = candidate selected (source 'selected'; question wording not deposited); 104 rows coded 999 (missing) dropped; 161 pairs with neither candidate selected kept as recorded (opt-out unknown). cov_failed_conjoint marks the 10 respondents the author drops; cov_flood_exposed = the author's treatment (damage level > 2). Spanish level text as in the data labels.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "If you had to decide: Which of the two proposals would you choose?" (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = "How much do you agree or disagree with proposal 1/2?" on 1-7, higher = more agreement (end labels not documented); both are the article's English of a German/French/Italian survey. Levels are the English text of the article's Table 1; level shares are unequal (e.g. year 2045 in 25% of profiles), so level weights are observed; no combination of levels is excluded; attribute order was randomized per respondent but not recorded; frame arm in trial_frame.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which nominee do you prefer to fill a vacancy on the Supreme Court?", prefaced in the treatment arms by "Assuming the Supreme Court is split 4-4" or "... composed of a 6-2 Republican [Democrat] majority" (arm in trial_court); forced choice, no opt-out. Partisanship (Independent 10%) and race (White 50%, Asian American 10%) were drawn with unequal weights. 9,359 conjoint completers; the paper's n = 9,895 includes 536 who did not finish.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Suppose you are voting in a primary election between two Republican candidates who are running for Congress. Which candidate do you prefer?" Candidate 1 / Candidate 2, no opt-out. Shown only to Republican and Independent identifiers (cov_party_id). Randomization restrictions and level weights undocumented; level shares in the table are near uniform. All 1,883 respondents with an answered task kept; the authors use good completes (cov_good_complete = 1, 1,481). No survey weights deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which candidate would you prefer to vote for?' forced choice of two profiles; rating = 1-7 per profile (1 definitely would NOT vote for, 7 definitely would vote for). Each respondent saw a randomly assigned number of filler attributes (trial_n_fillers), drawn at random from a pool; fillers not shown are '(not shown)'. Core attributes always shown; attribute order randomized but not recorded. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; the authors' recoded concordance variables dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which hotel room do you prefer? (paraphrase)' forced choice of two profiles; rating = 1-7 per profile (anchors not documented). Each respondent saw a randomly assigned number of filler attributes (trial_n_fillers), drawn at random from a pool; fillers not shown are '(not shown)'. Core attributes always shown; attribute order randomized but not recorded. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed; the authors' recoded concordance variables dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = preferred candidate of two (forced choice; wording not published, paraphrase). 60 tasks in four 15-task within-subject conditions (trial_condition): Normal excludes odd attribute combinations, the others allow incongruent and/or nonsensical ones, so estimators must account for the condition-specific restrictions; level shares are unequal. Lab sample (145 of 147 participants in this file); no respondent covariates deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = preferred immigrant of two (forced choice; wording not published, paraphrase). 60 tasks in four 15-task within-subject conditions (trial_condition): Normal excludes odd attribute combinations, the others allow incongruent and/or nonsensical ones, so estimators must account for the condition-specific restrictions; level shares are unequal. Lab sample (142 of 147 participants in this file); no respondent covariates deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Given a choice between these two profiles, which person would you prefer as a leader?" (forced A/B); rating: suitability of each profile, 1 = absolutely unsuitable to 5 = absolutely suitable ("an ideal leader for you"). Restrictions undocumented but some levels have unequal shares (Military, Kandahar, age 28). All four pre-conjoint prime arms kept (trial_prime); place-name free text dropped. N = 2,485 matches the codebook.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating: probability of voting for each candidate, 0 (would never vote for) to 10 (would definitely vote for), stored 0-10 (source 1-11); choice: forced choice 'Imagina que hay elecciones en tu municipio. ¿Qué alcalde o alcaldesa preferirías...' (García/Martínez), no opt-out. Fully randomized, no restrictions; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. The authors drop fast tasks (page time < 15/10/9 s for tasks 1/2/3, in trial_page_seconds); all tasks kept here.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Based on this information, which ONE of these two MPs would you prefer to have as your MP?" (MP 1 / MP 2, response required, no opt-out). Attributes assigned randomly and independently (full factorial of 768 profiles). Constituency, browser/device and derived recodes dropped; N = 1,719 matches the article and local-roots AMCEs (10-13 points vs living elsewhere) reproduce.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of the two candidates the respondent would rather vote for (article paraphrase), forced, no opt-out; 132 unanswered tasks omitted (20 respondents drop out; 1,485 of the article's 1,505). Priorities: exactly two of 12 per candidate, stored as one column per priority with "(not shown)" when absent; first/second order not in the deposit. Other restrictions and attribute order undocumented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which proposal would you prefer to be implemented?" (Proposal A / Proposal B, no don't-know option). Attribute order randomized per respondent and fixed across tasks (attrpos_; policy always first); restrictions undocumented. Level text is English (instrument labels; pricing, GDP and recommended-by abbreviated as in the article's Table 1) although respondents saw German. N = 1,558 matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two workers the respondent would prefer to receive greater government income assistance (forced choice, no opt-out); rating = 0-10 support for each worker receiving income assistance (0 strongly oppose, 10 strongly support). Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). Task 6 repeats task 1 with workers swapped, rebuilt from task 1 (trial_repeat_of = 1). trial_ict_info marks the between-subjects ICT information arm. All respondents with an answered task kept (4,013); the authors' 3,916 = cov_finished 1 and cov_duration_sec > 180.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Which candidate do you think would fare best in a [Democratic/Republican] primary in the area for which you are responsible as a party chairperson?', forced choice, no opt-out. Each profile showed a name plus 4 of 10 attribute rows drawn by a fixed scheme with non-uniform level weights (restriction); undrawn rows are '(not shown)'. Occupation, experience, military and descriptor levels are the authors' classes, not the displayed wording. The 0-100 'how much better' follow-up and noised county measures are not included.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "If you were living in this constituency at the next general election, which party would you vote for?" (current MP = profile 1, challenger = profile 2); opt-outs (third-party candidate, another party, would not vote) leave choice = 0 on both profiles in 4,305 of 9,810 tasks. The MP is always Labour or Conservative and the challenger a different party; the conduct line describes the MP only. Respondent party-identification flags dropped as derived; N = 1,962 matches the article and Table 1 col. 1 reproduces exactly.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = Q26 etc. vote (forced choice, Candidate A/B); choice_benefit_me / _prefecture / _japan = which candidate would bring more benefits to you personally / your prefecture / Japan (forced). Level text is Japanese as stored; piped fields not saved in the export are kept as placeholders ([respondent_prefecture], [outside_prefecture], [university_local], [university_outside], [todai_kyodai]), so text reads as design categories, not the names respondents saw. Restrictions undocumented; shares near uniform. 44 unfinished respondents kept (cov_finished = 0).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = vote (forced, Candidate A/B); choice_<issue> = which candidate would act more actively on business attraction, tourism, public works, government debt, diplomacy, pensions; choice_prefecture_issues = which would act more on the respondent's prefecture's issues. attr_local_status is the biography sentence as shown, with the respondent's own prefecture and universities filled in from the export's embedded fields (three designed versions: local, non-local, elite). Candidate gender fixed (male). 2 respondents without embedded values dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which candidate would you support?", forced (no opt-out), 7 tasks. Attribute text is the deposit's English label set; respondents saw their own language, and origin is stored as the authors' Born and Raised / Immigrated. Experience 0 and 10+ years and occupations lawyer and business had double randomization weight; about 86% of profiles are born and raised. Office (national/local) randomized except in US wave 2 (blank trial_office). 45 respondents without conjoint data dropped from the article's 14,369.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of Immigrant 1 / Immigrant 2 was chosen (forced choice; wording not deposited); rating = 1-7 rating of each immigrant (wording and anchors not deposited; higher = more favourable, inferred); rating_sim = a second 1-7 rating (ENGQ51, 'sim', meaning undocumented). Restrictions: high-skill professions only with university/postgraduate education; Russian ethnicity only with Russian-speaking language levels. Levels are the authors' English labels. All 3,000 respondents kept; the article analyses Muslim respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: respondents choose one of the two candidates (forced; exact wording not deposited). rating: each candidate on a 7-point scale, restored from the authors' 0-1 rescaling (rating2 * 6 + 1); higher = more favourable (chosen profiles rate higher), anchors unknown. Attribute order randomized but not recorded; no restrictions documented. All 4,012 respondents, matching the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Suppose that the following two parties were nominating candidates in this general election. Which party would you support? Even if you are not entirely sure, please indicate which of the two you would dare to support." (codebook translation of the Japanese), forced choice, no opt-out; unanswered tasks omitted. Attribute order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_, constant across a respondent's tasks); restrictions not documented, level shares near uniform. Sample filter as in the authors' code (fielding window, consent); 1,951 respondents, article N not checked.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of Contract A and Contract B the respondent would accept (paraphrase; forced choice, no opt-out). Five 2-level attributes randomly set each task; attribute row order randomized per respondent (not deposited). Task and profile are inferred from row order (task order assumed). Deposited sample = the authors' analysis sample after attention-check and completion exclusions; N matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of Contract A and Contract B the respondent would accept (paraphrase; forced choice, no opt-out). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of Contract A and Contract B the respondent would accept (paraphrase; forced choice, no opt-out). Deposited sample = the authors' analysis sample after attention-check and completion exclusions; N matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two government-response packages the respondent preferred (wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced choice, one chosen per pair. Attribute levels are the authors' English labels, not necessarily the text shown; randomization restrictions undocumented. Wave 1 of 2 (pre-NSL); cov_party_id is the respondent's political camp. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two government-response packages the respondent preferred (wording not deposited; paraphrase), forced choice, one chosen per pair. Attribute levels are the authors' English labels, not necessarily the text shown; randomization restrictions undocumented. Wave 2 of 2 (post-NSL); cov_party_id is the respondent's political camp. Qualtrics IDs re-keyed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice of the border plan the respondent would more likely support (wording paraphrased in the article), no opt-out; rating: each plan on an 11-point (0-10) scale, wording and anchors not given. Profile position was not deposited, so profile numbers are arbitrary. Level text is the article's English description of the German levels. No randomization restrictions stated. Respondent distance-to-border variables dropped (identifying).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: candidate selected (one per answered pair; wording not deposited); rating_qualified / rating_leadership / rating_implementation: 1-5 ratings of being qualified and suitable, leadership quality and task implementation (anchors not deposited; ratings correlate positively with selection). Restrictions and attribute order undocumented. 332 respondents in the deposit, 33 with no answers omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two curriculum-reform proposals the respondent supports (forced choice; exact wording not deposited). Faces are AI-generated images stored by file id, with the authors' coding of gender, age and ethnicity (attr_photo_*); the LGBT+/trans marker (a visual emoji cue) is stored as the authors' code. The foreign-country attribute is the country name as displayed; its framing (opposition/endorsement) is not deposited. Faces, names, countries, reasoning and proposals were not to repeat within a respondent. The deposit has 1,263 respondents; the article reports 1,358 for this country.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two curriculum-reform proposals the respondent supports (forced choice; exact wording not deposited). Faces are AI-generated images stored by file id, with the authors' coding of gender, age and ethnicity (attr_photo_*); the LGBT+/trans marker (a visual emoji cue) is stored as the authors' code. The foreign-country attribute is the country name as displayed; its framing (opposition/endorsement) is not deposited. Faces, names, countries, reasoning and proposals were not to repeat within a respondent. The deposit has 1,140 respondents; the article reports 1,169 for this country.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'At which of these destinations are you most interested in vacationing?' (Destination 1/2/3 or 'None of these destinations'; OPT-OUT, 16% of tasks have choice 0 on all three); rating = 'How interested are you in vacationing at each destination?' 1 Not at all interested to 5 Extremely interested (some blanks). 3 profiles per task; attribute order randomized and recorded (attrpos_). Unanswered tasks omitted; 2,076 respondents vs 'nearly 2,100' in the article. Two news levels lack the apostrophe in 'voters' (removed by the authors).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Would you prefer to read News Selection A or News Selection B?"; OPT-OUT in the abstention format only ("Neither": choice = 0 on both profiles, about 25% of abstention-format tasks); forced format has no opt-out. trial_arm / trial_format / trial_repeat_of identify the arm and the repeated 13th task. Two attributes (headline, source), row order randomized and recorded; restrictions undocumented. All respondents with an answered task kept (no screening applied, as in the authors' code).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "If this election were being held in your district, would you vote for Candidate A or Candidate B?" (forced format) or "... Candidate A, Candidate B, or neither candidate?" (abstention format, OPT-OUT: choice = 0 on both, about 26% of tasks); blank when only ratings were given. rating_shares_views / rating_good_morals / rating_cares: agreement that the candidate shares my views / has good morals / cares about people like me, 1 strongly disagree - 5 strongly agree. Characteristics hidden by the information environment are "(not shown)". Gender and race levels unequal (observed). No screening applied.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice_state: which firm would be better for the respondent's state (paraphrase of the authors' 'sociotropic' outcome); choice_family: which firm would be better for the respondent and their family (paraphrase, 'egotropic'); forced choice, no opt-out. Profiles come from 20 fixed design versions (trial_version), so only 223 of 960 profiles occur. Panel IDs, municipality identifiers and undocumented items dropped; N (2,008) not checked against the paywalled article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two museums (Museum A / Museum B) the respondent chose; forced choice, verbatim wording not deposited. Attribute levels are the authors' short Stata value labels, not necessarily the displayed text; cost is the stored dollar amount (the .dta cost labels are mis-attached). Randomization restrictions not documented, level shares uniform. One unanswered task dropped (2,315 tasks).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice of the candidate the respondent would rather vote for (article paraphrase), no opt-out. First and second priority are drawn from one list and never identical (restriction). Task and pair order inferred from row order. cov_survey_weight is the panel weight; thin-populism item wording/direction not deposited. Amended arm of the 2018 sample; the other half is neuner_2022_populist_candidates_2018.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice of the candidate the respondent would rather vote for (article paraphrase), no opt-out. First and second priority are drawn from one list and never identical (restriction). Task and pair order inferred from row order. cov_survey_weight is the panel weight; thin-populism item wording/direction not deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice of the candidate the respondent would rather vote for (article paraphrase), no opt-out. First and second priority are drawn from one list and never identical (restriction). Task and pair order inferred from row order. cov_survey_weight is the panel weight; thin-populism item wording/direction not deposited. Replication arm of the 2018 sample; the other half is neuner_2022_populist_amended_2018.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of the two security packages the respondent preferred (forced choice; wording paraphrased in the article); rating = each package on 1 strongly against - 5 strongly in favor. Attribute text is the English master (Table 1), not the national-language text shown; attribute order randomized per respondent but not recorded. Five countries pooled (cov_country, cov_survey_weight). Energy-framing arm of the same survey not included. 3,839 respondents vs 3,750 in the article; 2,893 pass the attention check.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = "How likely is it that you would vote for Candidate A [B]?" reversed from the source to 1 = very unlikely .. 5 = very likely (Ved ikke set missing); choice = "Hvilken kandidat foretrækker du?" with a Ved ikke opt-out (1,801 of 5,105 tasks have no chosen profile). Behavioral and symbolic localism were omitted for a random subset of profiles ("(not shown)"); five long localism levels are truncated at 80 characters in the deposit's labels. Gender, age, occupation and party follow the 2019 candidate distribution (non-uniform). All 1,021 respondents kept; the article analyses 779 after dropping speeders (cov_duration_sec < 180 s, 195 s with the prime, trial_prime).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these two candidates would you vote for as your MP?"; choice_others: "Which of these two candidates do you think others in your constituency would vote for as their MP?" Both forced choice, asked in random order (trial_self_first). Tasks with no recorded answer to one question have that outcome missing (25 and 56 tasks); tasks with neither are omitted. Attribute text is the authors' English labels; party = constituency winner (Major) / runner-up (Minor) / Independent, the actual names shown not deposited. trial_video is the randomized pre-conjoint video. Pilot dropped; 2,233 of the paper's 2,239 have answers.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these two political systems of government would you prefer the most?" (forced choice, OPTION 1 / OPTION 2). Unconstrained randomization except that the two profiles were never identical. Expats kept with cov_nationality (the author drops them; Egyptians = 1,000 matches the article); 3 tasks with no choice and 3 with two chosen profiles dropped. Level text English; most respondents saw Arabic.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Which of these two political systems of government would you prefer the most?" (forced choice, OPTION 1 / OPTION 2). Unconstrained randomization except that the two profiles were never identical. Expats kept with cov_nationality (the author drops them; Moroccans = 991 matches the article); 1 task with no choice and 1 with two chosen profiles dropped. Level text English; most respondents saw Arabic.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "If you had to choose between one of the two strategies, which would you personally prefer?" (translated from the German master questionnaire; forced, no opt-out). rating: each strategy on 1-7, 1 = definitely reject, 7 = definitely support (endpoint order randomized; reversed half recoded as in the author's code), asked in 2 of 4 tasks only. Attributes uniformly randomized without restrictions per the article; ties kept. All 2,334 respondents kept, matching the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which person would you contact first to offer a place in your list?' (English questionnaire; asked in Arabic), forced choice between two aspirants, 3 rounds; 103 unanswered rounds omitted and 11 candidates with no answered round dropped (1,896 of 1,907). Levels stored in Arabic as shown; the profession level 'وظيفة عمومية' (public-sector job) is labelled 'lawyer' in the author's code and questionnaire. Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). Restrictions undocumented. cov_ = candidate's list type and party membership.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two roommates was chosen (wording unknown), no opt-out; rating: each roommate 1-7, higher = more favourable (chosen profiles rate higher), anchors unknown. Task/profile inferred from row order and verified (one choice per pair). Sexual orientation LGBT drawn with probability 1/5 (authors' design); race shares also unequal. 203 of 205 respondents kept (2 with no saved attributes); article N not checked.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Em qual dos candidatos você votaria?" between Candidato A and B, forced (no opt-out); 3 tasks. Nine binary attributes independently randomized; the abortion attribute offers only keep current laws vs complete ban. The three policy attributes were shown first or last (trial_order); order within blocks randomized but not recorded. 1,817 respondents = the article's valid N after its filter (IP in country, consent, citizen, resident, 18+, finished). Questionnaire codes for covariates differ by country.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "¿Por cuál de los candidatos votaría usted?" between Candidato A and B, forced (no opt-out); 3 tasks. Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "¿Por cuál de los candidatos votaría usted?" between Candidato A and B, forced (no opt-out); 3 tasks.
