Gender and caste were each signalled by a name plus a category word; the table stores the category words. 2 respondents with no condition and 6 with no outcome dropped; N 2,360 vs 2,347 in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Paired choice between two trade agreements (Agreement A, Agreement B or Neither; Neither = opt-out, 411 tasks) and a rating of each agreement 1 (not favourably at all) to 10 (very favourably); wording paraphrased from the article. Respondents are interest groups, not individuals. 5 tasks with no answer omitted.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Choice-based conjoint: 'Please choose the protein source that you think is more sustainable on the basis of the information at your disposal' (English translation), two cards plus a 'no choice' option (opt-out; both cards 0). Fixed orthogonal design, the same 16 pairs for everyone; nutritional score, ecological score and price were each shown or not ((not shown)), with shown values fixed by product. Task order as displayed is not documented. All 639 respondents kept; the article excludes 98 (under 18 or diet due to disease) to reach 541.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment, real and incentivized: 'choose which of the two seeds you would purchase if you were at the market to buy seed. If you wouldn't buy either then choose ninguna' (enumerator script); ninguna = opt-out (both 0). Seed shown only as the plot symbol (circle = certified, square = QDS, triangle = recycled, blind to farmers). Fixed 12-pair design in four display orders. 2 farmers without a choice set and 2 invalid answers dropped. Price barely affects choice.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Incentivized referendum DCE: 'Which option do you vote for?' with a fixed 'No project' option (opt-out, all profiles 0). Three randomized formats in trial_mechanism: single binary (one project vs none, 600), sequential binary (9 questions, 300), sequential trinary (Project A vs Project B vs none, 9 questions, 300). Projects are 9 fixed bundles (fixed design); cost $5/$8/$11/$15 random. task = display order; trial_question = question number. Prolific IDs dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two development projects ('Which project do you prefer for your municipality?'), no opt-out, 4 tasks; 36 unanswered tasks omitted. Levels are the paper's English Table 1 text mapped from the deposit's short labels. Profile position inferred from the deposit's stacked row order (which project was shown first is assumed). Attribute order randomized per respondent, not recorded. Municipality ID dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice 'Which of these two birth scenarios would you choose?' between two hospital births of a first child (sex, out-of-pocket expenses $250-$10,000, birth weight 5 lb 8 oz-8 lb 13 oz, season), 7 tasks, no opt-out; orthogonal balanced main-effects design, attribute order randomized once per respondent. All 2,005 responses kept; the article's analysis sample of 1,894 is cov_main_sample = 1 (the rest were outside the US by IP, failed a repeated question or took under 2 minutes).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-proposal referendum vote 'Stimmen Sie diesem Vorschlag zu?' (Ja / Nein / Ich möchte nicht abstimmen): choice = Ja, choice_against = Nein, abstention 0 on both (opt-out); 6 proposals per respondent in a fixed order of rising levy, justification and differentiation randomized between respondents, levy rows depend on the justification. The codebook's vote coding (0 = yes) contradicts the authors' code and the data; 1 = yes is used. All 3,169 kept; the article drops the fastest and slowest 5% by survey time.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text vignettes in 3 pairs (French). choice: "Which politician are you most likely to vote for?" (forced, no opt-out); rating_represents, rating_trust, rating_capable (0-10 scales) stored as code 1-11 = displayed 0 (Pas du tout) .. 10 (Oui, tout à fait). Sub-Saharan African background shown about twice as often as each other background; 182 Turkish-background profiles carry North-African first names. Religion level 'pratique l'Islam'/'pratique l'islam' differs only in capitalisation by background, as stored. Part 3a profiles dropped. N = 1,199.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Agreement 1-5 (Muy en desacuerdo ... Muy de acuerdo) with '¿Qué tan de acuerdo estaría usted con pagar más impuestos <tax> para que el gobierno pueda aumentar el gasto público <area>?' (experiment 1, Q36). One sentence per respondent with two randomized clauses (control = clause omitted, '(not shown)'); Spanish clause text from the bilingual questionnaire. Pollfish online sample, Mexico, Dec 2021-Jan 2022, n = 2,401; no weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Agreement 1-5 with a proposal 'De acuerdo con una propuesta reciente <party>, el presidente debe retirar a los militares de las funciones de seguridad pública y buscar otras maneras para reducir el crimen <collaboration>' (experiment 4, Q46; the English column says 'national government' where the Spanish says 'el presidente'). One sentence per respondent with two randomized clauses (control = clause omitted, '(not shown)'); Spanish clause text from the bilingual questionnaire. Pollfish online sample, Mexico, Dec 2021-Jan 2022, n = 2,401; no weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Agreement 1-5 with 'Para reducir y controlar el crimen <territory>, se necesitan a más fuerzas de seguridad en las calles <measure>' (experiment 5, Q26; the article's experiment). One sentence per respondent with two randomized clauses (control = clause omitted, '(not shown)'); Spanish clause text from the bilingual questionnaire. Pollfish online sample, Mexico, Dec 2021-Jan 2022, n = 2,401; no weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two ratings of the same sentence 'Suponga que el gobierno recluta a más policías municipales <gender> <background>': rating = faith they would catch criminals (1 Nada ... 4 Mucho), rating_misconduct = likelihood of bribery, torture etc. (1 Nada probable ... 4 Muy probable; higher = less favourable) (experiment 6, Q15/Q16). Gender is either stated as female or not mentioned. One sentence per respondent with two randomized clauses (control = clause omitted, '(not shown)'); Spanish clause text from the bilingual questionnaire. Pollfish online sample, Mexico, Dec 2021-Jan 2022, n = 2,401; no weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw Dutch or French). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw German). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw Greek). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw English). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw Portuguese). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two hypothetical parties the respondent would vote for in national legislative elections (forced, no opt-out); rating: probability of voting for each party, 0 (definitely would not) to 10 (definitely would). 2 tasks, attribute order randomized per respondent; level text is the codebook's English wording (respondents saw Spanish). Respondents with blank attribute values dropped. One of six country tables (lobo_2023_parties_*).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two climate-policy packages (German wording not deposited; the US instrument asks 'Which policy package do you prefer?'), no opt-out; rating: 1-7 per package, wording and anchors not deposited, stored raw. 4 rounds x 2 packages, 6 attributes; 'No restrictions' appears twice as often as each specific restriction. No weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two climate-policy packages ('Which policy package do you prefer?', choose the one you oppose less if you support neither), no opt-out; rating: 1-7 per package, wording and anchors not deposited, stored raw. 4 rounds x 2 packages, 6 attributes; 'No restrictions' appears twice as often as each specific restriction. 93 incomplete single-package tasks dropped (1,350 of 1,360 respondents kept). No weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five paired scenario tasks; choice = forced choice of the scenario that would make the respondent more inclined to have a child (no opt-out; 399 tasks without a choice keep their ratings), rating = the respondent's intention to have a child within the next three years under each scenario, 1-10 (paraphrase; wording not deposited). Levels are the authors' short labels; income is the amount shown in local currency. Four countries pooled (cov_country); N = 8,330 (press release 8,334).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Quale tra questi due partiti voterebbe?' (forced, no opt-out); rating: agreement with each party agenda, 0 (per niente) to 10 (totalmente). Task 9 repeats task 1 with the two columns swapped (trial_repeat_of = 1; 69% consistent). Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). Respondents without a task-1 choice dropped, as in the authors' code; covariates are numeric codes without a codebook.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which candidate do you prefer?' (Candidate A or B, forced, one per task); rating_feeling = feeling thermometer for each candidate, 0 very unfavorable to 100 very favorable. Two rounds. Level text is the displayed text from the Qualtrics export. 13 answered tasks with unsaved profiles dropped (865 respondents vs 868 in the paper). Agreeableness (cov_agree_1-10, raw) and authoritarianism items kept; demographics as unlabelled codes.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating is the share of a fixed $10 million relief budget (in $ million, 0-10) given to each of two counties; the two ratings of a task sum to 10 (no choice column, no opt-out). Presidential partisanship is randomized per task and the same for both counties; county attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). cov_survey_weight is the authors' entropy-balancing weight used in the main results.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three forced choices per pair of crisis news reports (options 'The government in Crisis 1/2', no opt-out): choice 'Which government do you prefer to re-elect?', choice_handled 'Which government has handled their crisis better?', choice_responsible 'Which government is more responsible for the severity of their crisis?'. Attribute order fixed; levels as inserted into the report text. 12 partial respondents kept (the article's N = 812 completes). Prolific IDs dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two EU sanction proposals (no opt-out); rating: support for each proposal, 1 (no support) to 7 (high support). Task and profile inferred from row order (verified: exactly one chosen profile per pair). Attribute text is the deposit's short English value labels; question wording paraphrased (article not seen).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two EU sanction proposals (no opt-out); rating: support for each proposal, 1 (no support) to 7 (high support). Task and profile inferred from row order (verified: exactly one chosen profile per pair). Attribute text is the deposit's short English value labels; question wording paraphrased (article not seen).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two EU sanction proposals (no opt-out); rating: support for each proposal, 1 (no support) to 7 (high support). Task and profile inferred from row order (verified: exactly one chosen profile per pair). Attribute text is the deposit's short English value labels; question wording paraphrased (article not seen).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text conjoint: choice of which of two described politicians would better represent the respondent ('Welcher dieser Politiker würde Sie ihrer Meinung nach besser in der Politik vertreten?'), forced, no opt-out. Sentence order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_); the policy issue is shared within a pair and only the stance varies; ethnicity and sexuality levels have unequal probabilities by design. Attention-check failures and speeders are kept, flagged in cov_attention_pass and cov_duration_sec (the article drops them).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text conjoint: choice of which of two described politicians would better represent the respondent ('Which of these politicians do you think would better represent you in politics?'), forced, no opt-out. Sentence order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_); the policy issue is shared within a pair and only the stance varies; ethnicity and sexuality levels have unequal probabilities by design. Attention-check failures and speeders are kept, flagged in cov_attention_pass and cov_duration_sec (the article drops them).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Text conjoint: choice of which of two described politicians would better represent the respondent ('Which of these politicians do you think would better represent you in politics?'), forced, no opt-out. Sentence order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_); the policy issue is shared within a pair and only the stance varies; ethnicity and sexuality levels have unequal probabilities by design. Attention-check failures and speeders are kept, flagged in cov_attention_pass and cov_duration_sec (the article drops them).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Qual prefeito você prefere?' (forced, no opt-out); rating: performance of each mayor and rating_federal: performance of the federal government (asked once per task, repeated on both profiles), both 7-point Péssimo (1) to Ótimo (7). Attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_); 105 respondents have 3 tasks and 3 have 2; survey weight kept; Qualtrics ids re-keyed.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette survey, one vignette per task. rating_interview and rating_employ: 'How likely is that you will invite this person for the interview / that this person would be employed ...', 0 very unlikely to 10 very likely (codebook's 1-10 is wrong). rating_final_comparison keeps raw d2 codes: 0 not in the final pairwise comparison of the two highest-d11 candidates, 1 best (preferred), 2 second best. Fixed blocked design (144 vignettes in 24 decks); natives are always host-educated and C2-proficient by design. Level text is the English codebook labels; 'other ethnic group' resolved to the country's nationality per the codebook.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: "Based on the information above, which of the following two candidates would you be more likely to support?" Candidate 1 / Candidate 2, no opt-out. Candidate race and gender are shown only through names (gender crosswalk from the authors' candidate_names.xlsx). Platform-row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). 3 respondents with unsaved levels dropped; the authors' filters (US resident, not insincere) leave 573 of 622.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two candidates the respondent supports (YouGov 'Conjoint screen <k> candidate choice', Candidate 1 / Candidate 2; wording not in the codebook), no opt-out. Candidate race and gender are shown only through names. YouGov weight in cov_survey_weight. The authors drop respondents who answer surveys insincerely most of the time or always (cov_take_serious).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two candidates the respondent supports (YouGov 'Conjoint screen <k> candidate choice'; wording not in the codebook), no opt-out. Candidate race and gender are shown only through names. YouGov weight in cov_survey_weight. October 2018 appendix sample; the authors drop insincere respondents (cov_take_serious).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four candidates per screen, one per party (Die Linke, SPD, CDU, AfD; attr_party): choice of one candidate (no opt-out) and a 1-7 favourability rating of each (7 = most favorable). Level sets differ by party (the AfD candidate never has several terms of experience or the two liberal refugee policies) and each screen has one or two likely winners, so effects should be estimated within party. Attribute text is the codebook's English translation.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two leader profiles the respondent chose (wording not deposited; forced, one per task); choice_vote: follow-up 'would vote for selected profile' (No/Yes) coded 1 on the chosen profile if Yes, so opt-out (9,276 of 14,436 tasks have none). Attribute text is the authors' English labels of Finnish displays; profiles from 180 fixed design versions; typed age kept only when a whole number; municipality dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose, which of the two studies would you say is more ethical?' 1/2, forced (no opt-out). Attribute order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_ columns; attributes move in fixed blocks); unanswered tasks dropped, leaving 247 of 362 consenting respondents; ranking and harm batteries not kept.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between two federal arrangements (question wording not deposited); no opt-out. Task inferred from row order (A,B,A,B per respondent; every pair has one chosen profile). 102 of 2,108 pairs dropped for missing attributes or outcome; Endline and Expansion samples pooled as in the authors' code (cov_sample).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette survey, ECLS initiation scenario, 5 vignettes per respondent. rating_self 'From my point of view, ECLS/ECMO should be used in this patient', rating_clinic 'In my clinic, ECLS/ECLS would be used in this patient', 1 not correct at all to 6 fully correct (translated). Fixed blocked design; 80- and 90-year-old patients never bridged to transplant. Task is not display order (not recorded). Deposit has 510 respondents vs 420 analysed in the article (exclusions not applied). Level text is the article's English vignette wording.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette survey, ECLS withdrawal scenario, 5 vignettes per respondent. rating_self 'From my point of view, the ECLS/ECLS treatment should be discontinued', rating_clinic 'In my clinic, the ECLS/ECLS treatment would be discontinued', 1 not correct at all to 6 fully correct (translated); higher = more readiness to withdraw. Fixed blocked design; 80- and 90-year-old patients never bridged to transplant. Task is not display order (not recorded). Deposit has 467 respondents vs 420 analysed in the article. Level text is the article's English vignette wording.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single profile per round. choice: 'Please indicate whether you think YES this Government Leader should be re-elected or NO...' (1 = YES; NO is the opt-out); rating: 1 (Very Strongly Oppose) to 7 (Very Strongly Support) re-election. Pooled 16 countries with cov_country; attribute text is the English display text (translations shown outside English-speaking countries); 221 Brazilian rounds with a mistranslated jobs level dropped; respondents 22,180 vs 22,147 in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment, 5 tasks of OPTION A vs OPTION B ('Please check the option that suits you best'), forced choice, no opt-out; rating_confidence = 'To what extent are you confident with your choice?' 0-100 (task level). Czech labels; cost and value attributes stored as the percentage behind the amount shown. Only the Czech online sample (N = 1,531) is built; the Polish online and both face-to-face samples of the deposit are held for data defects.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose, which proposal would you prefer the government to pursue?' Proposal A/B, forced (no opt-out). Randomized introduction (coal-decline information or not) in trial_intro; cov_survey_weight is the trimmed raking weight that reproduces SI Table 8.1 (the deposited code uses the untrimmed weights2, kept as cov_weight_untrimmed); one unanswered task dropped; 248 respondents as in the SI.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose, which proposal would you prefer the government to pursue?' Proposal A/B, forced (no opt-out). Randomized introduction (coal-decline information or not) in trial_intro; authors' raking weight in cov_survey_weight (trimmed version in cov_weight_trimmed); ZIP codes and panel ids dropped; 1,001 respondents as in SI Table 4.1.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two CDU candidates the respondent prefers (codebook 'Candidate choice'; paraphrase), forced, no opt-out; rating: candidate thermometer -5..+5 as stored (higher = more positive). Levels are the stored German labels. Saxony, Thuringia and Western Germany samples pooled (cov_survey_region). 45 unanswered rounds dropped; panel ids dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If these two candidates were running against each other for MLA, and the election were held today, which would you vote for?' (forced choice, no opt-out); candidates shown as drawings with surname, title and an appeal read aloud; party (BJP vs RJD) shown only in tasks 3-4, '(not shown)' elsewhere. Task/profile inferred from row blocks; the authors' binary StrongPref recode, 18 incomplete or off-pattern tasks and one empty respondent dropped (1,999 of ~2,000 respondents).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose a policy mix for Germany, which of the two options would you prefer?' (forced, no opt-out); rating: 'And how would you rate the two options?' 1 very negative - 7 very positive (English translation). 7 tasks, 4 attributes, all combinations allowed, attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_*); attribute text is the paper's English translation. All 2,211 respondents kept; the paper's main results use attention passers (cov_attention_pass = 1).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-vignette rating: how likely the described scenario is to be considered discriminatory, 1 (almost certainly not discriminatory) to 6 (almost certainly discriminatory); no choice, no opt-out. Each target attribute (gender, nationality, sexuality, education) appears once per respondent in random order and the displayed phrases are fixed by target x group status, so combinations are restricted; attr_ text is the article's English translation of the Japanese phrases; between-respondent definition arm in trial_definition; open-ended reasons dropped; 4,000 respondents as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One text vignette per respondent; rating = support for the surveillance measure (1 do not support it at all - 10 strongly support it), plus rating_efficacy, rating_restrict, rating_concern_personal, rating_concern_society (1-10; wording paraphrased from the preregistration). No choice, no opt-out; full factorial with equal-probability assignment; attribute levels are the author's labels because the German vignette text is not deposited; control levels are (not shown). N = 2,045 as in the article; post-treatment fear item dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette (one news story per respondent, 6 randomized factors, full factorial). rating: "If you were deciding this case, would you" definitely side with the school .. definitely side with the gay teacher, 4 points stored as the author's 0-1 recode (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1); rating_similar: 7-point slider 'Not at all similar' .. 'Extremely similar' stored as k/7; rating_lgb_jobs: support for laws protecting LGB people against job discrimination, 4 points recoded 0-1 (a general policy item asked after the story). No opt-out. Levels are the author's labels, not the story text. Straight respondents only; the four survey waves are pooled and not identified; the author's LGB-rights index is dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two tax-reform proposals the respondent prefers (paraphrase: 'choose which is most preferred'), forced, no opt-out; 6 tasks, 4 attributes (tax type, rate 1-20%, government services, institutional political influence), levels as the authors' value labels (respondents saw Chinese). 57 respondents with no choices omitted; the article's screened sample = cov_elite_t10 non-missing. Taiwan shadow-case file not built (tasks not recoverable).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Survey 1 (conjoint only). choice: Policy A vs Policy B (forced; wording not deposited, paraphrase). Attribute text from the embedded display strings; bots and attention-check failures were removed by the authors before deposit; 776 respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Survey 2: respondents randomized to one of four status retention/loss vignettes (trial_arm) before the conjoint. choice: Policy A vs Policy B (forced; wording not deposited). Unanswered tasks omitted (3,228 of 3,240 respondents kept); authors' manipulation and attention checks kept as cov_ flags; free text not included.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four forced choices on the same pairs of protests, names from the authors' files (exact wording not deposited): choice_sympathy (more sympathy), choice_policy (support for the protesters' policy demands), choice_disorder (more of a public disorder), choice_deserving (protesters more deserving); exactly one profile chosen per task. Attribute levels are the displayed sentence fragments; attribute order fixed. Q3.1 and race kept as unlabelled codes. Respondent count not checked against the paywalled article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Forced choice between Individual A and B (question wording not in the deposit), no opt-out, 5 tasks; Greek attribute text as exported (feminine/masculine forms are separate levels); gender and skin tone stored as the authors' English codes, apparently shown by photo. Observed restriction: 'very good Greek & English' only with residence in Greece without a permit. All 2,007 respondents kept (authors' Study 2 drops 3 with no weight); cov_survey_weight = deposited raking weight weight_new.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between hypothetical Society A and Society B (wording not deposited; paraphrase), no opt-out; 4 tasks, 4 attributes each drawn from 9 values ($ incomes for bottom 20%/middle 60%/top 20%, % upward mobility); screens also showed the computed average income and 90/10 ratio (not stored). trial_framing distant/nearby society (80/20, per respondent). Source A/B column labels are swapped against the README; positions inferred. Full sample of 1,458 kept with cov_preferred_sample for the article's 1,249 and both raked weights.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five pairs of cyberattack scenarios shown side by side, no choice asked; rating_confidence: 'how confident are you in the intelligence community's assessment of who was responsible for each attack?' 0 (not confident)-100 (complete confidence); rating_severity: 0 (not severe)-100 (very severe); rating_support_*: Would support (1) / Would not support (0) for six measures against foreign perpetrators or six sentences for US perpetrators (display logic, NA on the other kind). Perpetrator type x origin restricted (observed: terrorists only from Iran/Russia/US, government agencies never from the US). Authors' sample: 1,233 after consistency and straight-lining drops; derived dummies dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two policy schemes (attitudes toward highly skilled immigrants), no opt-out, refusals NA; rating: 0-10 rating of each scheme (dictionary says 1-10; anchors not deposited). Profile order inferred from row order; nationality 'mainland Chinese only' never paired with a 40,000/year quota (observed); attribute text in Chinese; survey question wording and the paper's N not verified.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: forced choice between two policy schemes (attitudes toward highly skilled immigrants), no opt-out, refusals NA; rating: 0-10 rating of each scheme (dictionary says 1-10; anchors not deposited). Profile order inferred from row order; nationality 'mainland Chinese only' never paired with a 40,000/year quota (observed); attribute text in Chinese; survey question wording and the paper's N not verified.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Each official rated 2 feedback messages on each of 3 local issues: rating_informative (1 Not informative - 4 Very informative) and rating_influential (1 Not influential - 4 Very influential), wording paraphrased; no choice. Position is the same for both messages of an issue and constituent/argument levels are issue-specific; the order of issues is not recorded (task = issue). 573 officials with ratings (149 with no saved attributes dropped).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four forced choices between two destination cities (choice; wording paraphrased, no opt-out; 67 unanswered pairs kept as NA where ratings exist) plus ten per-city 0/1 judgements (rating_*, e.g. fear discrimination, government protects immigrants), five asked in each of two randomized question versions (cov_question_version). Attribute row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). 1,164 respondents with an outcome (the authors' d.full.conjoint, 1,165; completes 1,112); survey weight kept where the deposit has one.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Which of these two candidates would you be more likely to vote for?', forced, no opt-out; rating: 1-7 per candidate, wording and anchors not deposited (stored raw; correlates positively with being chosen). Six tasks, 8 fully randomized attributes, row order randomized per task (attrpos_). Level shares unequal (Straight 2/3, Healthy 3/7, White 2/3, Not religious 1/2). Mechanism items dropped (undocumented 0 code); tasks without a recorded choice dropped. Six tasks in the file vs five in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Which of these two candidates would you be more likely to vote for?', forced, no opt-out; rating: 1-7 per candidate, wording and anchors not deposited (stored raw; correlates positively with being chosen). Five tasks, 8 fully randomized attributes, row order randomized per task (attrpos_). Level shares unequal (Straight 2/3, Healthy 3/7, White 1/2, Not religious 1/2). Mechanism items dropped (undocumented 0 code); tasks without a recorded choice dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Which of these two candidates would you be more likely to vote for?', forced, no opt-out; rating: 1-7 per candidate, wording and anchors not deposited (stored raw; correlates positively with being chosen). Five tasks, 8 fully randomized attributes, row order randomized per task (attrpos_). Level shares unequal (Straight 2/3, Healthy 3/7; other attributes near-uniform). Mechanism items dropped (undocumented 0 code); tasks without a recorded choice dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two Facebook-use situations the respondent picks (question wording not deposited), forced, 7 tasks from one of 4 fixed blocks; 2 attributes, levels are the author's English variable names, not the displayed German text. Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: choice = which of two providers the caretaker would choose (forced choice, no opt-out; wording not deposited). Fixed blocked design in three versions, each showing kindness, quality, name type and one of medicines/fee/time; attributes outside a version are '(not shown)'. Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: in each of 10 tasks, choose the renewable energy community offer (choice = 1) or stay with the current electricity supplier (choice = 0; opt-out, no attributes besides the current cost). Fixed blocked design of 40 sets in 4 blocks. Cost level stored as the relative text without the respondent-specific euro amount shown on screen.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Of the two charities above, which do you expect the government to adopt the flexible regulation instead of rigid regulation?' forced choice, no opt-out; rating: 'To what extent do you support the government to adopt the flexible regulation for Charity A [B]?' 1-7, higher = more support. Text from the English translation (fielded in Chinese). One task per charity field (trial_field), task number = field. Only Experiment 2 of the questionnaire is deposited.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Which of these two policies do you prefer?' Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single nominee profiles, six per respondent; rating = support ('On a scale from strongly oppose to strongly support...'), rating_qualified, rating_trust, each 5-point answer text coded 1-5, higher = more favourable. Between-subject arms (trial_arm): party leaning shown (partisan) or '(not shown)' (nonpartisan); attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five paired candidate tasks with two Turkish-text attributes (judicial-oversight law, social-policy plan); choice = which candidate the respondent would select (paraphrase; no opt-out; 231 tasks unanswered), rating_democrat = how democratic the candidate is, 0-10, rating_like = support for the candidate, 1-5 (paraphrases; anchors not deposited). trial_version marks the arm in which the oversight laws carry a gridlock or corruption justification. 510 of 515 respondents answered; the authors' 5 speeders are kept (cov_time_min).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Level text = codebook labels, displayed wording undocumented. Student sample, 713 respondents.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = member chosen as the more attractive access target (codebook paraphrase), forced pick of 2; rating = five-point interest in meeting the member, 1-5 as stored (anchors undocumented; higher = more interest by its relation to choice). Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three paired forced-choice tasks (3 attributes, displayed sentences); choice = preferred department (paraphrase), no opt-out. Follow-up hours-of-effort items (asked only for the chosen profile) are stored as unlabelled codes and not kept. N = 559 after dropping 3 incomplete surveys, as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Three paired forced-choice tasks (4 attributes, displayed sentences); choice = preferred project (paraphrase), no opt-out. Follow-up hours-of-effort items (asked only for the chosen profile) are stored as unlabelled codes and not kept. N = 559 after dropping 3 incomplete surveys, as in the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Ten paired job-offer tasks with nine displayed-text attributes, order randomized per respondent; choice = which job the respondent would take (paraphrase; forced, no opt-out), rating = each job on a 4-point scale stored raw, 1 = favourable end (direction inferred from agreement with the choice; anchors not deposited). YouGov weight in cov_survey_weight; N = 1,200.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which of two candidates the respondent preferred (no opt-out; 4 tasks without a recorded choice keep their ratings); rating_favor: 7-point favorability (higher = more favorable, anchors not documented); rating_ideology: perceived ideology 1 extremely liberal to 7 extremely conservative. Each respondent answered one of the two ratings (346 favorability, 344 ideology). Exact question wording, sample source and fielding date are not documented in the deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). DCE, choice: 'Bitte wählen Sie eine der beiden Varianten eines Online-Therapieprogramms, die Sie bevorzugen würden:' (OPTION A / OPTION B), no opt-out, 16 fixed choice sets (Bayesian D-efficient design, one block). German displayed level text from the codebook. Respondents were randomized to one of two context scenarios (trial_c_0001, code meaning undocumented). 20 unanswered tasks dropped; 2,004 respondents vs 1,984 analysed in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five single-profile tasks; rating = 'What punishment, if any, do you think they should receive?' 1 = a warning ... 13 = more than 30 years in jail (answer position, higher = harsher); rating_good_cause = 'How likely do you think it is that this individual was protesting for a good cause?' 1 = extremely unlikely to 5 = extremely likely. Task order inferred from row order; residence stored as the authors' group label (state piped into displayed text not saved); perpetrator race nonuniform by design. The double-profile experiment in the deposit is not built (pairs not recoverable). N = 3,402 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: which officer in each pair would make the respondent the most afraid (paraphrase of the preprint; Officer A / Officer B), forced choice, 5 tasks. Levels randomized independently; attribute order randomized per respondent and held across tables (attrpos_). General-population and Black oversamples pooled with the authors' combined weight; 14 unanswered tasks dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Pictured two-officer team, race (White/Latino/Black) and sex of each officer and stop location (empty/busy street) randomized; one picture per respondent. rating_hurt/force/weapon/arrest: 'Afraid these officers will -- physically hurt you / use excessive force against you / point a weapon at you / wrongfully arrest you', raw 1 = Very Afraid to 5 = Very Unafraid. Two samples pooled with the authors' combined weight.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two paired tasks, 4 attributes (Dutch text as displayed); choice = 'Aan welk participatie initiatief zou je het liefst willen deelnemen?' (forced, Initiatief 1/2); choice_results, choice_process, choice_trust = which initiative would give the best results / the best process / most trust in the government, each with a 'Geen verschil' (no difference) opt-out. French-language respondents (457) dropped because their displayed text is not saved; N = 683.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose, which candidate would you vote for?' (Candidate A or B, no opt-out). Subjects were randomly assigned to see party, ideology and previous office in addition to the 5 finance attributes (trial_arm; '(not shown)' otherwise). 437 rounds missing one profile in the deposit (implausible donation combinations apparently removed after fielding) are dropped; the candidate approval rating is not in the deposit.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose, would you vote for or against this initiative?' (For = Support campaign profile chosen, Against = Opposition; no opt-out); rating: approval of each side of the campaign, 1 strongly disapprove to 7 strongly approve. Issue display order not saved (task follows a fixed issue order). 103 rounds missing one campaign in the deposit are dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: respondent's pick between two hypothetical coyotes (question wording not deposited; codebook: 1 = this profile was chosen), forced choice, up to 3 tasks. Levels are the authors' English short labels; the displayed text is not deposited. 549 unanswered tasks dropped; 1,415 of 1,534 respondent ids answered at least one task.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Up to two paired tasks (trial_forum principal, then stakeholder) with five binary attributes described by the codebook's English level text; choice = which demand to prioritize (paraphrase; wording not deposited), forced, no opt-out. Task inferred from row order; 9 respondents have one pair only. N = 385 respondents, 761 decisions as in the article; no rows dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment, 14 tasks of two unlabelled policy alternatives; choice = forced choice between alternative 1 and 2 (wording not deposited), rating_certainty = certainty about the choice, 1 = very uncertain to 5 = very certain (asked per task, repeated on both rows). Levels are the codebook values (patient deaths x 1,000, signed; premium change in euros per month), not displayed text. Fixed blocked design; task = design scenario number. N = 708 as in README.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Dual-response discrete choice experiment, 10 tasks; choice = stage-2 choice among alternative 1, 2 and a constant third alternative (current situation: 1,200 deaths, no premium change, good condition; stored as profile 3), choice_stage1 = forced choice between alternatives 1 and 2 (profile 3 not offered, 0). Wording not deposited; levels are codebook values (deaths x 100, premium change in euros per month, quality good/moderate). Survey arms 1-3 undocumented. N = 691 as in README.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Welchen Plan würden Sie bevorzugen?' Forced choice, 5 tasks of 2 climate policy plans, German level text. Respondents were first randomized to one of three vignettes (trial_vignette: Control / Compensation Treatment / Carbon Tax Treatment; texts not deposited). Restrictions and attribute order undocumented. Sample = authors' attention-check passers who finished (2,191); postcode, free text and platform ids dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'Welche dieser beiden Kandidaten/Kandidatinnen würden Sie in der kommenden Bundestagswahl eher wählen? Bitte wählen Sie einen Kandidaten/eine Kandidatin aus, selbst wenn Ihnen keine der beiden Optionen gefällt.' Forced choice, 5 tasks of 2 candidates, German level text. Energy policy levels unequally weighted (current speed 40%); restrictions and attribute order undocumented. Sample = authors' attention-check passers who finished (2,191); postcode, free-text comments and Qualtrics/panel ids dropped; two full dates of birth set missing.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment, choice = the issue the respondent would choose to prioritize (article paraphrase), 2 issues per set, 4 sets, no opt-out; fixed blocked design, domain (roads or schools) per respondent in trial_service. Level text = the article's English Table 2 wording mapped from Included/Not Included codes (displayed in Dutch/French). Age and tenure dropped (re-identification risk).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice: 'If you had to choose between them, which of these candidates would you vote for?' (Candidate A or B, no opt-out); rating: trustworthiness of each candidate, 1 (Not at all) to 5 (Extremely). Respondents voted in their own party's primary (trial_primary; independents assigned at random); Democratic candidates never 'Strongly opposes' and Republican candidates never 'Strongly Supports' the two policies. Contests with missing or duplicated rows dropped (8,870 kept vs 8,931 reported).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Up to four paired stakeholder tasks; choice = 'Which stakeholder's demand would you prioritize?' (forced choice, no opt-out). Level text from the article's Table 1 (English instrument; Dutch sample saw Dutch text, not deposited). Tasks with identical profiles were removed by the authors before deposit; 58 unanswered tasks dropped. UK and NL pooled (cov_country); 4,637 tasks match the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). DCE: choice = "Select your preferred journal" between Journal A and Journal B, no opt-out. Task 1 is a dominant set, tasks 2-9 the respondent's block of a fixed blocked efficient design, task 10 a retest of task 2 (or 3) with the same A/B order (inferred). Levels transcribed from the authors' choice-set images because the design files are not deposited. Two designs (trial_design 1 = first sample of 96, 2 = second sample of 520) and two scenarios (trial_scenario).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which of the two policies do you prefer?" (forced choice between Policy A and B, no opt-out), 5 tasks of 6 attributes; respondents first saw one of six randomized information treatments (trial_info_treatment). Survey in Chinese; attribute text is an English reconstruction and the USA partner levels omit their emission-share figure. No restrictions documented; level probabilities not documented.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which of the two policies do you prefer?" (forced choice between Policy A and B, no opt-out), 5 tasks of 6 attributes; respondents first saw one of six randomized information treatments (trial_info_treatment). No restrictions documented; level shares observed unequal.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two policy bundles the government should adopt and implement (forced, one per task); rating = 1-7 support for each bundle (1 strongly oppose, 7 strongly support). No opt-out; four attributes, randomized independently by the article, attribute order randomized once per respondent (not recorded). Profile position inferred from row order. Beijing sample of the same deposit not included (screen text unknown). N 1,501 (article: 750 per wave).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Paired candidates, 10 tasks + task 11 repeating task 1 (same positions; trial_repeat_of = 1); choice = 'Which candidate are you most likely to vote for?' (no opt-out); rating = 'Looking at just Candidate k, how likely are you to vote for this candidate for Congress?' 1 very unlikely - 5 very likely (authors' coding). Level probabilities unequal by design. All 1403 respondents with saved profiles and any answer are kept; the authors' filter (complete, reCAPTCHA >= 0.5, not a pure independent) leaves 1176; respondents with no saved attribute levels dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Paired candidates, 10 tasks + task 11 repeating task 1 (same positions; trial_repeat_of = 1); choice = 'Which candidate are you most likely to vote for?' (no opt-out); rating = 'Looking at just Candidate k, how likely are you to vote for this candidate for Congress?' 1 very unlikely - 5 very likely (authors' coding). Level probabilities unequal by design. All 1403 respondents with saved profiles and any answer are kept; the authors' filter (complete, reCAPTCHA >= 0.5, not a pure independent) leaves 1179; respondents with no saved attribute levels dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two paired scenario tasks; choice = the scenario in which the respondent would cooperate with the police (paraphrase; wording not deposited), forced choice, no opt-out. Levels are the authors' English labels (displayed wording not deposited); profile order within a task is the deposit's row order, screen position unknown. N = 1,841 (not checked against the closed article).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette (text), 5 topic vignettes per respondent, each randomizing speaker (professor/journalist), statement (conservative/progressive x with/without political demand) and a critical reaction ('(not shown)' when absent); four yes/no judgements stored as ratings (Ja = 1, Nein = 0): cancel the talk, revoke his teaching assignment, remove his book from the library, allow disruptive protests. Task numbers are topics, not display order (first four topics in random unrecorded order); 19 soft-launch respondents' item order corrected as in the authors' code. Studies 2-4 of the deposit are not built.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Of the two scenarios, in which case do you think it would be better for someone in the community rather than the police to punish the perpetrator directly?" and choice_punish = "which case do you think should be punished more severely?", both forced choice between Case 1 and Case 2, no opt-out. Attribute text is the authors' English factor labels (survey in Spanish); perpetrator labels differ slightly from the codebook's. Restrictions and attribute order not documented; N = 9,365 matches the abstract's "over 9000 households".

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five MP vignettes per respondent; rating_represented 'How well do you feel represented by this MP?' (1 not at all - 7 very well), rating_like_mp 'Every [nationality] MP should be like this MP' (1 strongly disagree - 7 strongly agree), rating_trait_* = traits chosen (up to 3) after the last vignette, on task 5 only. Bill direction and public opinion appear only in some information arms (trial_info_version) and are otherwise '(not shown)'; bill direction depends on the respondent's preference; free text and unlabelled items dropped; N = 14,000 as in the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Five forced choices per pair of corruption scenarios (Scenario A/B): which harms you and your family most, harms Armenia's economy more, reduces confidence in the political system more, is more morally wrong, happens more often (wording from the English instrument); 98/99 answers set to NA; no opt-out. Restricted randomization: favors to family and use of public resources for own firm occur only with personal use and keeping all funds; political use never with keeping all funds. Tasks with a mismatched screen number dropped. cov_survey_weight = authors' age x gender post-stratification weight. N 1,497 (authors 1,495).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Candidate ratings, no choice: each respondent was randomly assigned one outcome - rating_dominance ('aggressive, threatening, and intimidating'), rating_warmth ('warm, reliable, and friendly'), rating_competence ('competent, knowledgeable, and skillful'), each 7-point Strongly disagree to Strongly agree, or rating_vote (how likely to vote for the candidate) - stored rescaled 0-1 as deposited; Don't know omitted. Second Study 1 experiment only; non-uniform weights for age bands, gender and background by design.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: choice = which burger (Option A or B), forced, no opt-out; question wording not deposited. Fixed Bayesian-efficient design of 20 sets (plant-based and cell-cultured are one Type attribute); supermarket or restaurant framing randomized between respondents (trial_setting), with restaurant prices £10 higher. Level text taken from the choice-card images.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). 8 pairs of primary candidates per respondent; choice_electable = candidate identified as more electable, choice_vote = preferred candidate (paraphrase from codebook; questionnaire not deposited), forced choice, no documented opt-out. Ideology levels depend on the primary scenario (Democratic: very liberal/liberal/moderate; Republican: moderate/conservative/very conservative), district attributes are per pair; skipped pairs NA (authors' 0), 48 respondents without answers dropped; Qualtrics/panel ids and free text dropped; paper N not checked.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Article Experiment 3. rating: 'Please indicate to what extent you support giving foreign aid through each aid agency' 1 (strongly oppose) to 10 (strongly support), one rating per agency, one task of two agencies; no choice, no opt-out. Each attribute is a statement shown with Yes/No, independently randomized. Survey weight kept (cov_survey_weight). N = 2,058 matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Article Experiment 2. rating: 'Please indicate to what extent you support giving foreign aid through each aid agency' 1 (strongly oppose) to 10 (strongly support), one rating per agency, one task of two agencies; no choice, no opt-out. Each attribute is a statement shown with Yes/No, independently randomized. Survey weight kept (cov_survey_weight). N = 2,058 matches the article.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Paired contributions, 7 tasks; choice = forced choice between Contribution 1 and 2 (wording not reported, no opt-out); rating_amount = minimum worthwhile grant (million USD) and rating_overhead = overhead to charge (%), both open-text answers stored as the authors' numeric cleaning; rating_refuse = 1 if the respondent wrote 'No' (reject the contribution). Six binary features independently randomized; only respondents who completed all 7 pairs are in the deposit (280, as in the paper).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). DCE: choice = "Please select your preferred scenario" among Scenario 1, Scenario 2 and a business-as-usual scenario that displays its levels (profile 3; no separate opt-out). Fixed design of 16 cards answered by everyone, row order differs by card (attrpos_). Five countries pooled, English level text from the English questionnaire. Answer codes 1-3 inferred as the three columns.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which proposal do you prefer (Proposal 1 or Proposal 2)? Please choose one.", forced choice, no opt-out; 6 tasks, attribute row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). The status-quo marker " (SQ)" stored in the data was not displayed and is stripped; the free-text 'other group' answer and Qualtrics ids are dropped. N = 151 matches the paper; the state-representative presidency AMCEs (0.010, 0.011) reproduce.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One candidate vignette per respondent (2 x 3 x 2: PAC contributions, prior experience, gender); rating_vote 'Vote likelihood', rating_donate 'Donation likelihood', rating_trust 'Candidate trustworthiness' (paraphrase; wording not deposited), 7-point stored raw with 1 = Very likely/trustworthy and 7 = Very unlikely/untrustworthy. No opt-out; candidate party is matched to respondent party (trial_candidate_party); skipped answers NA; zip codes and panel ids dropped; N = 1,000 as in the authors' log.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Four paired tasks; choice = the social-assistance reform proposal the respondent preferred (paraphrase; wording not deposited), forced choice, no opt-out. Levels are the author's English labels of a Danish instrument (from the replication Rmd); attribute row order randomized per respondent (attrpos_); survey weight kept. N = 1,287 (not checked against the article).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two-step ranking of 3 fictitious publications per set: choice = picked first (no opt-out), rating_rank = 1 picked first, 2 picked second, 3 remaining (1 = most preferred; question wording not deposited). Fixed chained design of 20 sets, same for all; screen position not recorded. Set 1 or 2 is absent for 110 of 224 respondents (undocumented); a practice set and one task where the deposit's two files disagree are dropped; 224 respondents vs 247 participating in the abstract.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One factorial policy proposal per respondent; choice = 'Imagine you had to decide today only on this proposal in a popular vote, would you vote for or against it?' (1 = vote for; voting against is the opt-out), rating = 'Please indicate, how much do you support or oppose this proposal?' 1 strongly oppose to 7 strongly support. All 54 designs kept (the article analyses 12 'plausible' ones, n = 1,634); two instruction arms in trial_info_arm; raking weight kept; municipal accessibility score dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Study 1 (Taiwan). Three picks per pair of ballots: choice_fair, choice_democratic, choice_efficient ('which of the two ballots is more fair / democratic / efficient', paraphrase from variable names; wording not deposited); forced pick, unanswered picks NA. 7 fixed ballot designs crossing language (4) and arrangement (stacked/separated; monolingual ballot has none, '(not shown)'). Levels are the authors' English descriptions of Chinese ballot images. Demographic codes without codebook dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = forced choice between two policy packages (wording not deposited), no opt-out, one task per respondent with profile order inferred from row order and verified against the recorded choice; rating = the authors' 'Conjoint rank policy (1-7)', wording and direction undocumented, stored raw. Three prohibited level pairs (security x budgets, security x economy) per the authors' design code; levels are the authors' English (survey in Hebrew). The deposit's second (phase-2) conjoint is not built: numeric codes without displayed text.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Two ratings per election scenario, two scenarios per screen, 3 screens: rating = "How interested would you be in running in each election?" (1 Not interested - 5 Very interested) and rating_winprob = "If you were to run, how likely is it that you would win in each election?" (1 Very unlikely - 5 Very likely), coded from the option text; question order and option order randomized (cov_question_order, cov_answer_order). Opponent ideology was restricted to the side opposed to the respondent's self-placement; attribute order randomized per respondent (attrpos_). 745 respondents vs 734 responses in the preanalysis plan.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Single-profile text vignette, choice = "Given the information provided above, would you refer the patient to the ED or not refer?" (Refer = 1), not referring is the outside option (opt_out = yes); fixed blocked design, 6 vignettes per block (blocks 1 and 3), levels coded from the instrument's scenario texts. Task order follows the instrument (not recorded). 150 GPs answered all six scenarios; the record reports n = 142.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Discrete choice experiment: choice = preferred health service (Service A or B) for a child who is unwell, forced choice with no opt-out; fixed Bayesian-efficient design of 24 choice sets in 2 blocks of 12. Appointment-level text from the article (fielded grid not deposited); 458 respondents kept, the article analyses 450.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Generally speaking, if you had to choose, which one of these two options would you prefer?" (Option A / Option B / Don't know; Don't know is an opt-out, 3,805 tasks with no choice); rating = "how do you feel about it?" for each option, 1 like it a lot to 4 don't like it at all (Don't know -> NA). Tax rates across the five income brackets were restricted to non-decreasing schedules.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = preferred candidate of two (codebook 'Dummy whether respondent prefers candidate'; wording not deposited), one task, no opt-out; trial_competence_arm = 1 adds a competence/political-office sentence (attr_competence), '(not shown)' in arm 0. Attribute text is the German Qualtrics field text (encoding repaired); the authors' recoded policy factor mislabels candidate 2 in 745 of 1,000 tasks and the raw fields are used instead. Survey Experiment 1 (fixed-pair 2 x 2 vignette, wording not deposited) is not built.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = respondent prefers this hypothetical ward-leader candidate over the other (codebook paraphrase; original wording and language not deposited), no opt-out; 3 pairs per respondent, task inferred from row order and verified (one choice per pair), position within pair not recorded. Levels are the codebook's English descriptions. 1,704 of 7,878 respondents whose candidate traits were not saved are dropped.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette (one per respondent): six statements each shown with probability one-half after a fixed base text. rating = approval of the IMF program (1 disapprove a lot - 4 approve a lot); rating_gov_responsible and rating_imf_responsible = responsibility of the government / the IMF for the program (1 not - 3 much responsible); rating_imf_confidence = confidence in the IMF (0-10). Statement order in the vignette undocumented. cov_survey_weight = poststratification weight. N 1,691 (articles: 1,600; analysis sample 1,514).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). rating = "On a scale from 0 to 10, how FAIR do you think the impact of these policies would be in:" each of two countries, stored as the export's codes 1-11 (1 = 0 very unfair, 11 = 10 very fair); 5 tables per respondent, attribute order randomized per table. Table 4 used alternative row labels and mobility wording (trial_label_set). Duplicate Prolific submissions (2) dropped; 1,577 respondents vs 1,567 analysed in the article; speeders kept (cov_duration_sec).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette, one scenario per respondent (Study 3, 16 cells). rating: 'Reviewing the options above, which would you choose to assist you?' 1 = Definitely the expert to 7 = Definitely the algorithm; rating_agent: 'If you merely had to choose between either the expert or the algorithm, which would you choose?' 1 = The expert, 2 = The algorithm. No opt-out; full factorial, no restrictions. Free-text reasons, nationality and the authors' derived variables dropped; gender 'Other/don't want to tell' set to NA. N matches the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette, one scenario per respondent (Study 1, 16 cells). rating: 'Reviewing the options above, which would you choose to assist you?' 1 = Definitely the expert to 7 = Definitely the algorithm; rating_agent: 'If you merely had to choose between either the expert or the algorithm, which would you choose?' 1 = The expert, 2 = The algorithm. No opt-out; full factorial, no restrictions. Free-text reasons, nationality and the authors' derived variables dropped; gender 'Other/don't want to tell' set to NA. N matches the paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Factorial vignette, one incentivized scenario per respondent (16 cells, real GBP 1 investment). rating_agent: 'Please choose your option now' 1 = Option A: Expert, 2 = Option B: Algorithm; rating: 'Reviewing the options above, please tell us how strongly you prefer one option over the other for this investment.' 1 = I definitely prefer the expert to 7 = I definitely prefer the algorithm; rating_invest (only if the picked agent offered control): 1 = BUY!, 8 = ABORT!. No opt-out; full factorial. Prolific IDs, free text and derived variables dropped; gender 'Other/don't want to tell' set to NA. N = 210, no paper.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two cities the respondent would prefer to move to (Arabic question text from the export), forced, one per task; no opt-out. Six binary attributes, Arabic level text; attribute row order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_). Respondents who stopped part-way keep their answered tasks. N 735; article count not checked (paywalled).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = which of two cities the respondent would prefer to move to (Arabic question text from the export), forced, one per task; no opt-out. Six binary attributes, Arabic level text; attribute row order randomized once per respondent (attrpos_). Respondents who stopped part-way keep their answered tasks. N 4,322; article count not checked (paywalled).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One hypothetical trial-court judge profile per respondent (7 attributes, one value each randomly assigned, attribute order randomized but not recorded); rating = support for the judge, 1-5 strongly oppose to strongly support, rating_fairness = fairness, 1-5 very unfair to very fair; wording paraphrased from the README. Level text from article Table 1; partisanship level 'No partisan information provided' is Table 1's label. 71 respondents with no treatment/outcome omitted (962 of 1033).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). One hypothetical trial-court judge profile per respondent (7 attributes, one value each randomly assigned, attribute order randomized but not recorded); rating = support for the judge, 1-5 strongly oppose to strongly support; wording paraphrased from the README. Level text from article Table 1; partisanship level 'No partisan information provided' is Table 1's label. 52 respondents without the support item omitted (1172 of 1224).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which candidate do you prefer as President of the Republic?" (Candidate A / B, forced, no opt-out); rating = favourability of each candidate, 1 Very unfavorable to 10 Very favorable. 7 tasks, 9 two-level attributes randomized with randomized attribute order (order not recorded). Level text is the English Chile questionnaire wording (respondents saw Spanish); the tax level differs from the EU version.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = "Which candidate do you prefer as Chancellor?" (Germany; Prime Minister in Portugal) (Candidate A / B, forced, no opt-out); rating = favourability of each candidate, 1 Very unfavorable to 7 Very favorable. 7 tasks, 9 two-level attributes randomized with randomized attribute order (order not recorded). Germany, Portugal and the Netherlands pooled (cov_country); level text is the master English wording (respondents saw German, Portuguese or Dutch).

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). Labelled DCE, 2 blocks x 6 cards, four scheme alternatives plus 'No scheme' (opt-out: 54 tasks with no chosen profile); choice = 'Please choose your preferred scheme'; rating_land_share (chosen scheme only) = % of arable land or permanent grassland the respondent would enrol, 0-100. Payment levels are scheme-specific. Card contents transcribed from the questionnaire images. England sample only (N = 107, as in the article); German and Czech samples (<100 each) not included.

Conjoint table (irw_conjoint). choice = 'Which of the two proposals would you prefer?' (forced, no opt-out); rating_accept = whether the respondent accepts each proposal, 1 = yes, 0 = no (wording paraphrased). English level labels stored though most respondents answered in German, French or Italian; densification is the % increase in residents and cost rent the % of units at cost rent; postal codes and free text dropped; 3,500 respondents vs 3,497 in the article.
